    LY_ESYS,        /**< System call failure */
    LY_EINVAL,      /**< Invalid value */
    LY_EEXIST,      /**< Item already exists */
    LY_ENOTFOUND,   /**< Item does not exists */

    LY_EVALID,      /**< Validation failure */
    LY_EDENIED,     /**< Operation is not allowed */

                         This value is used ORed with one of the other LY_ERR value and can be simply masked. */

    LY_STMT_UNITS = 0x310000,
    LY_STMT_VALUE = 0x320000,
    LY_STMT_WHEN = 0x330000,
    LY_STMT_YANG_VERSION = 0x340000,
    LY_STMT_YIN_ELEMENT = 0x350000,

    LY_STMT_SYNTAX_SEMICOLON,
    LY_STMT_SYNTAX_LEFT_BRACE,
    LY_STMT_SYNTAX_RIGHT_BRACE,

    LY_STMT_ARG_TEXT,
    LY_STMT_ARG_VALUE
};
objects.description: Enumeration of YANG statements and some parser tokens. Values are bit masks for many entries, enabling masks like LY_STMT_DATA_NODE_MASK. Used across parsing/compilation APIs to identify substatements, parents, and storage kinds.
Generic parsed YANG substatement node used to represent unknown or plugin-specific statements within an extension instance. Forms a linked tree via next/child.
Descriptor for a known parsed substatement supported by an extension instance, carrying the statement kind and a pointer to where parsed storage should be written.

Parsed representation of a single YANG extension instance, including name/argument, parse-format context, parent info, supported known substatements, any plugin-private parsed data, generic child statements, and nested extension instances.
Descriptor for a known compiled substatement supported by an extension instance, holding the statement kind and pointer to compiled storage location.
Compiled representation of a YANG extension instance with link to extension definition, module, nested instances, parent info, compiled substatements array, and plugin-private compiled data.
Plugin vtable for implementing a YANG extension. Holds identifiers and optional callbacks for parse/compile, printers, data helpers, validators, and free/serialization hooks.
Registry record binding a specific extension (module/revision/name) to its plugin implementation callbacks. Used to expose plugins via LYPLG_EXTENSIONS macro.
Enumeration describing how LYB-encoded values report their size: fixed in bits, variable in bits, or variable rounded to bytes.

objects.definition:

    lyplg_type_store_clb store;         /**< Storing and canonization callback for the value. */
    lyplg_type_validate_value_clb validate_value;   /**< Optional value validation callback. */

    lyplg_type_compare_clb compare;     /**< Comparison callback for comparing 2 values of the same type. */

    lyplg_type_print_clb print;         /**< Printer callback for getting value representation in any format. */

};

Function pointer type for callbacks that validate stored values against the accessible data tree.

objects.definition: struct ly_ht;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a libyang hash table instance. Only a forward declaration is provided in this header; the structure layout is private to the library. Instances are created with lyht_new(), duplicated with lyht_dup(), and destroyed with lyht_free().

objects.definition: typedef ly_bool (*lyht_value_equal_cb)(void *val1_p, void *val2_p, ly_bool mod, void *cb_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for value-equality callbacks used by the hash table. The callback receives two value pointers (val1_p is the searched/inserted/removed value, val2_p is a value stored in the table), a mod flag indicating whether the operation modifies the table, and user data. It must return true when values are considered equal.

Typedef for an unsigned 32-bit integer used for version components. Note: This type is not defined in this header; it is a standard C fixed-width integer typedef provided by <stdint.h> or equivalent via included headers. Included here for clarity only if considered built-in; per instructions, types merely referenced but not defined should be ignored.

functions.name: ly_ctx_new
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_new(const char *search_dir, uint32_t options, struct ly_ctx **new_ctx);
functions.description: Create a new libyang context holding schemas and shared runtime state. Typical entry point; most applications use a single context for all work. Returns LY_SUCCESS and sets *new_ctx on success.
requirements: new_ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the created context on success.
search_dir may be NULL or a colon-separated list of directories (semicolon on Windows) to search for modules.
options is a bitmask of context options (see contextoptions); some options may affect behavior globally or compilation state.
Caller must eventually destroy the context with ly_ctx_destroy().
Function returns LY_ERR; caller must check the return value before using *new_ctx.

functions.name: ly_ctx_new_ylpath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_new_ylpath(const char *search_dir, const char *path, LYD_FORMAT format, int options,        struct ly_ctx **ctx);
functions.description: Create or augment a libyang context based on yang-library data loaded from a file at path. Loads modules listed in the yang-library into the context, sets features accordingly, and otherwise behaves like ly_ctx_new().
requirements: ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer. If *ctx is NULL, a new context is created and returned; if *ctx is not NULL, the existing context is modified.
path must point to a file containing yang-library data; must not be NULL.
format must specify the yang-library data format (LYD_FORMAT).
search_dir may be NULL; when provided, it is used to search for modules (yang-library module paths in the data are ignored).
options is a bitmask of context options (see contextoptions).
Only the first module-set from the yang-library is processed; the preferred yang-library tree revision is 2019-01-04, with legacy fallback if needed.
Caller must check LY_ERR return value before using/assuming changes.

functions.name: ly_ctx_new_ylmem
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_new_ylmem(const char *search_dir, const char *data, LYD_FORMAT format, int options,        struct ly_ctx **ctx);
functions.description: Create or augment a libyang context based on yang-library data provided as an in-memory string. Loads modules listed in the data and sets features accordingly.
requirements: ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer. If *ctx is NULL, a new context is created; otherwise the existing context is modified.
data must be a non-NULL string with yang-library data in the specified format.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT describing the provided data.
search_dir may be NULL; used to search for modules, ignoring paths embedded in yang-library data.
options is a bitmask of context options (see contextoptions).
Only the first module-set from the yang-library is processed; preferred revision is 2019-01-04 with legacy fallback.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_new_yldata
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_new_yldata(const char *search_dir, const struct lyd_node *tree, int options,        struct ly_ctx **ctx);
functions.description: Create or augment a libyang context based on a provided yang-library data tree (lyd_node). Loads modules referenced by the tree and sets features accordingly.
requirements: ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer. If *ctx is NULL, a new context is created; otherwise the existing context is modified.
tree must be a non-NULL data tree pointing to yang-library data.
search_dir may be NULL; used to search for modules, ignoring paths embedded in yang-library data.
options is a bitmask of context options (see contextoptions).
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value before using/assuming changes.

functions.name: ly_ctx_compile
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_compile(struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Compile (or recompile) the context to apply any pending changes. Only meaningful if LY_CTX_EXPLICIT_COMPILE option is set; otherwise it has no effect.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
Use this after changes (module additions, feature changes, etc.) when LY_CTX_EXPLICIT_COMPILE is enabled.
Caller must check LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_set_searchdir
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_set_searchdir(struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *search_dir);
functions.description: Add a search directory to the context’s set of schema search paths. The set can be reset with ly_ctx_unset_searchdir().
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
search_dir must be a non-NULL path string to add.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_unset_searchdir
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_unset_searchdir(struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *value);
functions.description: Remove specific search directory entries from the context, or remove all when value is NULL.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
value may be NULL to remove all search directories; otherwise must be a path string to remove.
To remove the most recently added entries by count, use ly_ctx_unset_searchdir_last().
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_unset_searchdir_last
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_unset_searchdir_last(struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t count);
functions.description: Remove the least recently added search directories by count. Removing more than present removes all and is not an error; 0 does nothing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
count is the number of entries to remove; 0 has no effect; values greater than the number of entries remove all.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_searchdirs
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const char * const *ly_ctx_get_searchdirs(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return a NULL-terminated array of the context’s search directories. The returned array and strings must not be modified.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
The returned array is owned by the context; caller must not modify or free it.
The return may be NULL if no search path was set.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_options
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t ly_ctx_get_options(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Get the current context options bitmask.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: ly_ctx_set_options
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_set_options(struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t option);
functions.description: Set (enable) the specified context options. May trigger recompilation and overwrite lysc_node.priv when toggling LY_CTX_SET_PRIV_PARSED.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
option is a bitmask of options to set (see contextoptions).
Changing LY_CTX_SET_PRIV_PARSED causes context recompilation and overwrites all lysc_node.priv; user must not change private objects when LY_CTX_SET_PRIV_PARSED is set.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_unset_options
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_unset_options(struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t option);
functions.description: Unset (disable) the specified context options.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
option is a bitmask of options to unset (see contextoptions).
Caller must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_change_count
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint16_t ly_ctx_get_change_count(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return the lifetime change count of the context’s module set.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_modules_hash
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t ly_ctx_get_modules_hash(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return a hash representing all modules in the context (names, revisions, enabled features, and implemented/imported state). Order-independent.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_imp_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL ly_module_imp_clb ly_ctx_get_module_imp_clb(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, void **user_data);
functions.description: Get the custom callback used to retrieve missing imported/included modules, and optionally the associated user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
user_data may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the callback’s user data.
Returns NULL if no callback is set.

functions.name: ly_ctx_set_module_imp_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_ctx_set_module_imp_clb(struct ly_ctx *ctx, ly_module_imp_clb clb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Set a callback used to retrieve missing imported/included modules (used when modules are not locally available).
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
clb may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise must conform to ly_module_imp_clb signature.
user_data is stored and passed back to clb whenever it is invoked.

functions.name: ly_ctx_set_ext_data_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL ly_ext_data_clb ly_ctx_set_ext_data_clb(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, ly_ext_data_clb clb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Set a callback providing run-time data for extension instances. For internal extensions like ietf-yang-schema-mount, the callback must return the expected data type (e.g., operational tree with required nodes). Returns the previously set callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
clb may be NULL to clear; otherwise must conform to ly_ext_data_clb signature.
user_data is stored and passed back to clb whenever invoked.
Caller should ensure the callback returns data consistent with the specific extension’s expectations (e.g., validated mount data for schema-mount).

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *name, const char *revision);
functions.description: Get a module by name and optional revision from the context. If revision is NULL, a no-revision module is returned if present.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL module name string.
revision may be NULL or a revision date string.
Returns NULL if no matching module exists.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_latest
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_latest(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *name);
functions.description: Get the latest available revision of the named module in the context. Modules with no revision are considered the oldest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL module name string.
Returns NULL if no module of that name is present.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_implemented
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_implemented(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *name);
functions.description: Get the only implemented revision of the named module in the context, if any.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL module name string.
Returns NULL if no implemented revision exists.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_iter
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_iter(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t *index);
functions.description: Iterate over all modules in the context. Pass index=0 to start, and call repeatedly to traverse. Returns NULL when done.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
index must be a valid non-NULL pointer; initialize to 0 to start iteration and reuse across calls.
Do not modify returned modules through this API unless allowed elsewhere.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_ns
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_ns(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *ns, const char *revision);
functions.description: Get a module by XML namespace and optional revision from the context. If revision is NULL, a no-revision module is returned if present.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
ns must be a non-NULL namespace string.
revision may be NULL or a revision date string.
Returns NULL if no matching module exists.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_latest_ns
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_latest_ns(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *ns);
functions.description: Get the latest available revision of the module identified by its namespace. Modules with no revision are considered the oldest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
ns must be a non-NULL namespace string.
Returns NULL if no module with that namespace is present.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_module_implemented_ns
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_get_module_implemented_ns(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *ns);
functions.description: Get the implemented revision of the module identified by its namespace, if any.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
ns must be a non-NULL namespace string.
Returns NULL if no implemented revision exists.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_submodule
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct lysp_submodule *ly_ctx_get_submodule(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *submodule,        const char *revision);
functions.description: Find a submodule by name and optional revision anywhere in the context. If the belongs-to module is known, prefer ly_ctx_get_submodule2().
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
submodule must be a non-NULL submodule name string.
revision may be NULL or a revision date string.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_submodule_latest
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct lysp_submodule *ly_ctx_get_submodule_latest(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *submodule);
functions.description: Find the latest revision of a submodule by name anywhere in the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
submodule must be a non-NULL submodule name string.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_submodule2
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct lysp_submodule *ly_ctx_get_submodule2(const struct lys_module *module, const char *submodule,        const char *revision);
functions.description: Find a submodule by name and optional revision within a specific parent (belongs-to) module.
requirements: module must be a valid non-NULL module pointer.
submodule must be a non-NULL submodule name string.
revision may be NULL or a revision date string.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_submodule2_latest
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct lysp_submodule *ly_ctx_get_submodule2_latest(const struct lys_module *module,        const char *submodule);
functions.description: Find the latest revision of a submodule by name within a specific parent module.
requirements: module must be a valid non-NULL module pointer.
submodule must be a non-NULL submodule name string.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: ly_ctx_internal_modules_count
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t ly_ctx_internal_modules_count(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return the number of internal modules (loaded during context creation).
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: ly_ctx_load_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lys_module *ly_ctx_load_module(struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *name, const char *revision,        const char **features);
functions.description: Search for and load a module into the context (using either search paths or a custom missing-module callback). If revision is NULL, the latest is loaded unless an implemented revision is already present, in which case that implemented revision is returned.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL module name string.
revision may be NULL or a revision date string.

features may be NULL, or a NULL-terminated array of strings. Special cases: a single string "*" enables all features; an array of length 1 containing only the terminating NULL explicitly disables all features.
Returns NULL on error or if not found; otherwise returns the loaded/selected module.
Caller should be aware that multiple implemented revisions of the same module are not allowed in a context.

functions.name: ly_ctx_get_yanglib_data
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_get_yanglib_data(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct lyd_node **root,        const char *content_id_format, ...);
functions.description: Generate ietf-yang-library data describing all modules in the context and return it as a lyd_node tree in *root. Datastore list instances are not created and must be appended by the caller. Optionally format the content-id using printf-like content_id_format and args.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
The ietf-yang-library module must be loaded in the context; otherwise the function returns an error (e.g., LY_EINVAL when disabled by LY_CTX_NO_YANGLIBRARY).
root must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the generated tree on success.

content_id_format may be a printf-like format string; when used, corresponding variadic arguments must match the format. Suggested patterns include "%u" with ly_ctx_get_change_count() or ly_ctx_get_modules_hash().
Caller must check LY_ERR return value before using *root.
The function creates a single /ietf-yang-library:yang-library/schema instance with key "complete"; caller must append /datastore list instances if needed.

functions.name: ly_ctx_free_parsed
functions.signature: LIBYANG_APIDECL void ly_ctx_free_parsed(struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Free all parsed modules in the context to reduce memory usage. Some schema functionality will no longer work afterward, but data manipulation remains possible.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
Caller must understand that certain schema-dependent functionality becomes unavailable after this call.

functions.name: ly_ctx_compiled_size
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL int ly_ctx_compiled_size(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return the total size required to serialize the compiled context. Returns -1 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 as an error.

functions.name: ly_ctx_compiled_print
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_compiled_print(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, void *mem, void **mem_end);
functions.description: Serialize (print) the compiled part of a context into a pre-allocated memory block (e.g., from mmap). Only compiled modules are printed; the result is immutable and read-only.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer to a compiled context.
mem must be a valid non-NULL writable memory block large enough to hold the printed context (size obtainable via ly_ctx_compiled_size()).
mem_end may be NULL or a pointer to receive the address immediately after the printed context.
Caller must check LY_ERR return value.
The memory should be reused at the same absolute address when later creating a printed context with ly_ctx_new_printed().

functions.name: ly_ctx_new_printed
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_ctx_new_printed(const void *mem, struct ly_ctx **ctx);
functions.description: Create an immutable context that directly uses previously printed compiled context structures from a memory block. Allows one printed context per thread per memory address at a time.
requirements: mem must point to a memory region previously filled by ly_ctx_compiled_print(), at the exact same absolute address.
ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer; on success, *ctx receives the created immutable context.
This function enforces that a given thread can create only one printed context at a particular memory address at any time (another thread may create one at the same address).
Caller must check LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: ly_ctx_is_printed
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL ly_bool ly_ctx_is_printed(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Determine whether the context was created from a printed (immutable) context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: ly_ctx_destroy
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_ctx_destroy(struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Destroy the context and free all its internal structures. Modules are freed automatically. Instance data should be freed beforehand. User data stored in lysc_node.priv are not freed by libyang.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect) or a valid context pointer to destroy.
All instance data associated with the context should be freed before destroying the context (e.g., with lyd_free_all()).
User-owned private data stored in lysc_node.priv are not freed by this function; caller is responsible for freeing them.

functions.name: lydict_insert
functions.signature: LY_ERR lydict_insert(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *value, size_t len, const char **str_p);
functions.description: Inserts a string into the libyang context dictionary. If the same byte sequence already exists, only its reference count is incremented and no new allocation occurs. Accepts non–NULL-terminated data when len > 0; a terminating NUL is added internally. If value is NULL, the function performs no operation. Use this when you want the dictionary to keep its own copy of the bytes.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid libyang context.
value may be NULL (no-op).
If len is 0, value must be a valid NUL-terminated string (strlen() is used).
If len > 0, value must reference at least len readable bytes; the data need not be NUL-terminated.
str_p may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the dictionary's canonical pointer for the stored string.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return code and handle LY_EINVAL (invalid parameters) and LY_EMEM (allocation failure).

functions.name: lydict_insert_zc
functions.signature: LY_ERR lydict_insert_zc(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, char *value, const char **str_p);
functions.description: Zero-copy insert of a NUL-terminated string into the libyang dictionary. If the string does not exist, the dictionary takes ownership of value (no duplication). If it already exists, the dictionary increments the refcount and frees value. After the call, the caller must not use value.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid libyang context.
value may be NULL (no-op).
value must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
value must be dynamically allocated and suitable for being freed by the dictionary when deduplicated (do not pass stack/static memory).
After calling, the caller must not access value regardless of return path (ownership may have been transferred or the memory freed).
str_p may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the dictionary's canonical pointer for the stored string.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return code and handle LY_EINVAL (invalid parameters) and LY_EMEM (allocation failure).

functions.name: lydict_remove
functions.signature: LY_ERR lydict_remove(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *value);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a string in the libyang dictionary and frees it when the count reaches zero. The match is by pointer identity (address) to a dictionary-managed string, not by string content. If value is NULL, the function does nothing.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid libyang context.
value may be NULL (no-op).
value must be a pointer previously obtained from the same dictionary (address must match an existing entry); passing an identical-but-different buffer will not be matched.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return code; LY_ENOTFOUND is returned if value is not a dictionary entry, LY_SUCCESS on successful decrement/removal.

functions.name: lydict_dup
functions.signature: LY_ERR lydict_dup(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *value, const char **str_p);
functions.description: Duplicates a dictionary string by incrementing its reference count. No new memory is allocated for the string data. Returns LY_ENOTFOUND if value is not found in the dictionary.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid libyang context.
value must be a NUL-terminated string pointer that already exists in the dictionary (typically previously returned by a dictionary API).
str_p may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the dictionary's canonical pointer for the stored string.
Caller must check the LY_ERR return code and handle LY_ENOTFOUND when value is not a dictionary entry.

functions.name: ly_in_type
functions.signature: LY_IN_TYPE ly_in_type(const struct ly_in *in);
functions.description: Return the type of the underlying input medium used by the ly_in handler. Use to branch logic depending on whether the handler reads from a file descriptor, FILE*, filepath, or memory.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in previously created by ly_in_new_*().
If in is invalid, the function may return LY_IN_ERROR (per enum documentation).

functions.name: ly_in_reset
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_reset(struct ly_in *in);
functions.description: Reset the input medium to its beginning so the next read starts from offset 0. On non-seekable inputs (e.g., pipe/FIFO/socket), the call succeeds but has no effect. The reset does not restore the exact original open state (for files, it seeks to 0, not to the original open offset).
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in.
Callers must handle LY_ESYS on failure.
Be aware that for non-seekable inputs the function has no effect even if it returns LY_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ly_in_new_fd
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_new_fd(int fd, struct ly_in **in);
functions.description: Create a new input handler that reads from an existing file descriptor. On success, returns LY_SUCCESS and stores the handler to *in.
requirements: in must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handler.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor positioned at the desired read offset.
Caller is responsible for eventually freeing the handler with ly_in_free().
On failure, do not use *in.

functions.name: ly_in_fd
functions.signature: int ly_in_fd(struct ly_in *in, int fd);
functions.description: Get or set the file descriptor associated with an existing input handler. If fd == -1, returns the current descriptor. If fd != -1, replaces the handler’s descriptor and returns the previous one.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in configured for FD input.
If fd != -1 and the call succeeds, the caller is responsible for closing the returned previous file descriptor.
Handle a return value of -1 as an error when attempting to set a new descriptor.

functions.name: ly_in_new_file
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_new_file(FILE *f, struct ly_in **in);
functions.description: Create a new input handler that reads from an existing FILE* stream. On success, returns LY_SUCCESS and stores the handler to *in.
requirements: in must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handler.
f must be a valid FILE* opened for reading and positioned at the desired read offset.
Caller is responsible for eventually freeing the handler with ly_in_free().
On failure, do not use *in.

functions.name: ly_in_file
functions.signature: FILE *ly_in_file(struct ly_in *in, FILE *f);
functions.description: Get or set the FILE* stream for an input handler. If f == NULL, returns the current FILE*. If f != NULL, attempts to replace the stream and returns the previous FILE* on success.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in configured for FILE input.
If f != NULL and the call succeeds, the caller is responsible for closing the returned previous FILE* stream.
If the function returns NULL, treat it as invalid argument or setup error; in this case the original handler in is untouched.

functions.name: ly_in_new_memory
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_new_memory(const char *str, struct ly_in **in);
functions.description: Create a new input handler that reads from a memory string. The string must be NULL-terminated. If ly_in_free() is later called with destroy = 1, the string will be freed with free().
requirements: in must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handler.
str must be a valid, NULL-terminated string containing the input data.
If you plan to call ly_in_free(in, 1), str must be dynamically allocated (not static/readonly) and compatible with free().

functions.name: ly_in_memory
functions.signature: const char *ly_in_memory(struct ly_in *in, const char *str);
functions.description: Get or change the memory buffer used by the input handler. If str is non-NULL, replaces the current buffer (must be NULL-terminated) and returns the previous starting address; if str is NULL, returns the current starting address.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in configured for MEMORY input.
If providing a new str, it must be a valid, NULL-terminated string.
When changing the buffer (str != NULL), the caller is responsible for freeing the previous data pointer that is returned (unless it will be freed later via ly_in_free(in, 1)).
Ensure the previous buffer was dynamically allocated if you intend to free it.

functions.name: ly_in_new_filepath
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_new_filepath(const char *filepath, size_t len, struct ly_in **in);
functions.description: Create a new input handler that opens and reads from the file at the provided path. If len == 0, filepath is treated as a NULL-terminated string; otherwise, exactly len bytes from filepath form the path.
requirements: in must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handler.
If len == 0, filepath must be a valid NULL-terminated string; if len > 0, filepath must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes of path characters.
Caller is responsible for freeing the handler with ly_in_free().

functions.name: ly_in_filepath
functions.signature: const char *ly_in_filepath(struct ly_in *in, const char *filepath, size_t len);
functions.description: Get or change the filepath used by the input handler. If filepath == NULL, returns the current filepath string. If changing (filepath != NULL), the current file is closed and a new one is opened; on success returns NULL, on failure returns (void*)-1.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in configured for FILEPATH input.
If len == 0, filepath must be a valid NULL-terminated string; if len > 0, filepath must contain at least len bytes.
When changing the filepath, be prepared that the underlying file is closed and a new one is opened instead of renaming the previous file.
Do not free the returned filepath string when just querying (ownership is not transferred).
Check the return value: NULL indicates success when changing; (void*)-1 indicates failure.

functions.name: ly_in_parsed
functions.signature: size_t ly_in_parsed(const struct ly_in *in);
functions.description: Return the number of bytes parsed by the last function that operated on this input handler. Useful for diagnostics or progress tracking.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in.

functions.name: ly_in_free
functions.signature: void ly_in_free(struct ly_in *in, ly_bool destroy);
functions.description: Free an input handler. If destroy is non-zero, also free/close the underlying input resource: for LY_IN_MEMORY, free() the input string; for LY_IN_FD and LY_IN_FILE, close the descriptor/stream.
requirements: in must be a valid ly_in (unknown whether NULL is accepted; treat NULL as unknown).
If destroy is non-zero and the input type is LY_IN_MEMORY, the original input string must be safe to pass to free().
If destroy is non-zero and the input type is LY_IN_FILE or LY_IN_FD, the underlying FILE*/fd will be closed; do not close it elsewhere afterward.

functions.name: ly_in_read
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_read(struct ly_in *in, void *buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Read count bytes from the input into buf. Newline counting is not performed; the caller is expected to count newlines if needed. Returns LY_SUCCESS on success or LY_EDENIED on EOF.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least count bytes (inferred from signature and typical I/O semantics).
count specifies the number of bytes to read; handle LY_EDENIED as EOF.

functions.name: ly_in_peek
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_peek(struct ly_in *in, uint8_t *peek);
functions.description: Peek the next byte from the input without consuming it for subsequent ly_in_read() or ly_in_skip(). Returns LY_ENOT if a byte has already been peeked and not yet read or skipped; returns LY_EDENIED on EOF.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in.
peek must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the next byte (inferred from being an out parameter).
If a byte has been peeked and not yet consumed (via ly_in_read or ly_in_skip), a subsequent ly_in_peek call will return LY_ENOT; callers should consume the prior peek before peeking again.
Handle LY_EDENIED as EOF.

functions.name: ly_in_skip
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_in_skip(struct ly_in *in, size_t count);
functions.description: Skip count bytes in the input without copying them out. Newline counting is not performed; the caller should count if needed. Returns LY_SUCCESS on success or LY_EDENIED on EOF.
requirements: in must point to a valid ly_in.
count is the number of bytes to skip; handle LY_EDENIED as EOF.

functions.name: ly_log_level
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_LOG_LEVEL ly_log_level(LY_LOG_LEVEL level);
functions.description: Set the global libyang logger verbosity level and return the previous level. Typical usage: set a new level and, if you need to read the current level without changing it, call the function, store the returned previous value, then immediately call it again with that previous value to restore.
requirements: level must be a valid LY_LOG_LEVEL value (one of LY_LLERR, LY_LLWRN, LY_LLVRB, LY_LLDBG).
To read the current log level without changing it permanently, call ly_log_level(), then call it again with the returned value to restore.

functions.name: ly_log_options
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t ly_log_options(uint32_t opts);
functions.description: Set the global logger options bitfield (default is LY_LOLOG | LY_LOSTORE_LAST) and return the previous options. Options control printing and storing of messages.
requirements: opts must be a bitfield composed of @ref logopts flags (LY_LOLOG, LY_LOSTORE, LY_LOSTORE_LAST).
To read the current logger options without changing them permanently, call ly_log_options(), then call it again with the returned value to restore.

functions.name: ly_temp_log_options
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t *ly_temp_log_options(uint32_t *opts);
functions.description: Set temporary, thread-safe logger options that override the global options set by ly_log_options(). Passing NULL restores the effect of the global options. Returns the previous temporary options pointer.
requirements: opts may be NULL to restore the global logger options.

If opts is non-NULL, it must point to a valid uint32_t containing a @ref logopts bitfield and the pointed storage must remain valid for as long as the temporary options are in effect (inferred from pointer semantics).

functions.name: ly_log_dbg_groups
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL uint32_t ly_log_dbg_groups(uint32_t dbg_groups);
functions.description: Enable specific categories of debug messages, independent of the log level. Returns the previously enabled debug-groups bitfield. Has no effect in non-debug (Release) builds.
requirements: dbg_groups must be a bitfield composed of debug groups (e.g., LY_LDGDICT, LY_LDGXPATH, LY_LDGDEPSETS).
This setting only takes effect in Debug builds; in Release builds it has no effect.

functions.name: ly_set_log_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_set_log_clb(ly_log_clb clb);
functions.description: Set the logging callback used by libyang to deliver log messages instead of printing to stderr. The callback receives level, message, optional data and schema paths, and an optional line number.
requirements: clb must be a function pointer matching the ly_log_clb signature: void (*)(LY_LOG_LEVEL, const char*, const char*, const char*, uint64_t).
Whether NULL is allowed to unset the callback is not explicitly documented; behavior when passing NULL is unknown.

functions.name: ly_get_log_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_APIDECL ly_log_clb ly_get_log_clb(void);
functions.description: Get the currently set logging callback. Can return NULL if no callback is set (messages will otherwise be printed according to options).

functions.name: ly_strerr
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const char *ly_strerr(LY_ERR err);
functions.description: Return a human-readable string describing the given libyang error code.
requirements: err should be a valid LY_ERR value.
The returned string is const; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: ly_strvecode
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const char *ly_strvecode(LY_VECODE vecode);
functions.description: Return a human-readable string describing the given validation error code.
requirements: vecode should be a valid LY_VECODE value.
The returned string is const; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: ly_last_logmsg
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const char *ly_last_logmsg(void);
functions.description: Get the last generated log message for the current thread, including any additional information such as paths or line where available.
requirements: The returned string is const; do not modify or free it.
Message is thread-specific; only reflects messages generated in the calling thread.

functions.name: ly_err_first
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct ly_err_item *ly_err_first(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return the first error-item structure recorded for the given context (thread- and context-specific), or NULL if none.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context (struct ly_ctx*) associated with the errors you want to inspect.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; treat as read-only and do not free.
Errors are stored per-thread and per-context; only errors generated in the calling thread for this ctx will be visible.

functions.name: ly_err_last
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const struct ly_err_item *ly_err_last(const struct ly_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Return the latest error-item structure recorded for the given context (thread- and context-specific), or NULL if none.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context (struct ly_ctx*).
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; treat as read-only and do not free.
Errors are stored per-thread and per-context; only errors generated in the calling thread for this ctx will be visible.

functions.name: ly_err_print
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_err_print(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct ly_err_item *eitem);
functions.description: Print the provided error-item as if it was just generated, optionally storing it in the given context according to logger settings.
requirements: ctx may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must be a valid libyang context that can store the message.
eitem must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid ly_err_item to be printed.

functions.name: ly_err_clean
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_err_clean(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct ly_err_item *eitem);
functions.description: Free error records stored in a context. If eitem is NULL, remove all error structures; otherwise, remove from the oldest up to and including eitem.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context whose error list will be modified.
eitem is optional; if provided, it must point to an error item belonging to ctx.
After this call, any freed ly_err_item pointers (including those returned earlier by ly_err_first/ly_err_last) must not be dereferenced.

functions.name: lyd_get_meta_value
functions.signature: static inline const char *lyd_get_meta_value(const struct lyd_meta *meta)
functions.description: Return the canonical (string) representation of a metadata node’s value. If meta is NULL, the function returns NULL. Otherwise, it uses the metadata’s stored canonical value if available, or computes it via the YANG context associated with the metadata’s annotation. The returned pointer is const and intended for read-only use; ownership/lifetime details are not documented here.
requirements: meta may be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL.

If meta is non-NULL, it must point to a valid, initialized struct lyd_meta produced/managed by the same libyang context, with meta->annotation, meta->annotation->module, and meta->annotation->module->ctx valid.
The metadata value (meta->value) must be initialized/valid.
The returned string must be treated as read-only by the caller; do not modify it.
Memory ownership and lifetime of the returned pointer are not specified here; the caller must not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: ly_out_type
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_OUT_TYPE ly_out_type(const struct ly_out *out);
functions.description: Return the output type associated with a libyang printer handler. Use to branch logic based on where output is directed (FD, FILE, memory, callback, etc.).
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.

functions.name: ly_out_reset
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_reset(struct ly_out *out);
functions.description: Reset the output medium to the beginning so subsequent prints rewrite existing content instead of appending. On non‑seekable outputs (pipes/FIFOs/sockets and callback outputs) this is a no‑op but returns success.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.
Behavior depends on underlying medium: non-seekable outputs will not actually be rewound.
The original content at handler creation is not restored; for files, offset 0 is sought and the file is truncated.

functions.name: ly_out_new_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_new_clb(ly_write_clb writeclb, void *user_data, struct ly_out **out);
functions.description: Create a printer handler that writes via a user-supplied write-like callback. Enables directing libyang output into arbitrary sinks.
requirements: writeclb must be a function compatible with ssize_t (*)(void *user_data, const void *buf, size_t count) that returns the number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to store the created handler.
user_data is opaque; it is passed to writeclb as provided.
On allocation failure, returns LY_EMEM and does not create a handler.

functions.name: ly_out_clb
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL ly_write_clb ly_out_clb(struct ly_out *out, ly_write_clb writeclb);
functions.description: Get or set the callback function of a callback-based printer handler. Returns the previous callback.
requirements: out must be a valid callback printer handler created by ly_out_new_clb().
If writeclb is NULL, the function only returns the current callback without changing it.

functions.name: ly_out_clb_arg
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void *ly_out_clb_arg(struct ly_out *out, void *arg);
functions.description: Get or set the user argument associated with a callback-based printer handler. Returns the previous argument value.
requirements: out must be a valid callback printer handler created by ly_out_new_clb().
If arg is NULL, the function only returns the current argument without changing it.

functions.name: ly_out_new_fd
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_new_fd(int fd, struct ly_out **out);
functions.description: Create a printer handler that writes to a file descriptor.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor suitable for writing.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to store the created handler.
On failure, returns an LY_ERR code and does not create a handler.

functions.name: ly_out_fd
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL int ly_out_fd(struct ly_out *out, int fd);
functions.description: Get or set the file descriptor used by an FD-based printer handler. Returns the previous descriptor on success.
requirements: out must be a valid FD/FDSTREAM printer handler created by ly_out_new_fd().
If fd is -1, the function does not change the descriptor and only returns the current one.
When changing the descriptor (fd != -1), the caller is responsible for closing the returned previous descriptor.
On error when setting a new descriptor, the function returns -1.

functions.name: ly_out_new_file
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_new_file(FILE *f, struct ly_out **out);
functions.description: Create a printer handler that writes to a FILE* stream.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to store the created handler.
On failure, returns an LY_ERR code and does not create a handler.

functions.name: ly_out_file
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL FILE *ly_out_file(struct ly_out *out, FILE *f);
functions.description: Get or set the FILE* stream used by a FILE-based printer handler. Returns the previous FILE* on change or the current one when querying.
requirements: out must be a valid FILE printer handler created by ly_out_new_file().
If f is NULL, the function only returns the current FILE* without changing it.
When setting a new stream (f != NULL), the caller is responsible for closing the returned previous stream.

functions.name: ly_out_new_memory
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_new_memory(char **strp, size_t size, struct ly_out **out);
functions.description: Create a printer handler that writes into a memory buffer. The buffer may be supplied by the caller or allocated/expanded internally.
requirements: strp is a pointer to a char* location where the resulting data pointer is stored.
If *strp points to an allocated buffer and size is set (non-zero), that buffer is used and may be extended.
If size is 0, a new buffer is allocated even if *strp points to an existing buffer.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to store the created handler.
On failure, returns an LY_ERR code and does not create a handler.

functions.name: ly_out_memory
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL char *ly_out_memory(struct ly_out *out, char **strp, size_t size);
functions.description: Get or set the memory buffer used by a memory-based printer handler. Returns the previous dumped data pointer when changing or the current one when querying.
requirements: out must be a valid MEMORY printer handler created by ly_out_new_memory().
If strp is NULL, the function ignores size and only returns the current dumped data pointer.
If strp is non-NULL and size is 0, a new buffer is allocated even if *strp points to an existing buffer (same rules as ly_out_new_memory()).
When changing the string pointer (strp non-NULL), the caller is responsible for freeing the returned previous dumped data.

functions.name: ly_out_new_filepath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_out_new_filepath(const char *filepath, struct ly_out **out);
functions.description: Create a printer handler that writes to a newly opened file at the given path. Note: header comment lines contain legacy/incorrect return description; the actual return type is LY_ERR as per the signature.
requirements: filepath must point to a valid path where the file can be created/opened for writing.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to store the created handler.
On failure, returns an LY_ERR code and does not create a handler.

functions.name: ly_out_filepath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL const char *ly_out_filepath(struct ly_out *out, const char *filepath);
functions.description: Get or change the filepath associated with a filepath-based printer handler. When changing, the current file is closed and a new one is opened (not renamed).
requirements: out must be a valid FILEPATH printer handler created by ly_out_new_filepath().
If and only if filepath is NULL, the function does not change the file and returns the current filepath string.
When changing the filepath (non-NULL), the current file is closed and a new one is opened.
Return semantics: previous filepath string is returned only when querying (filepath == NULL); when changing, returns NULL on success and ((void*)-1) on failure (cast to const char*).

functions.name: ly_print
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_print(struct ly_out *out, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Formatted print into the specified output (like fprintf/printf) using a libyang output handler. After calling, use ly_out_printed() to get the number of bytes printed.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.
format must be a valid printf-style format string with corresponding variadic arguments.
Check the LY_ERR return value; the number of bytes printed is available via ly_out_printed(out).

functions.name: ly_print_flush
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_print_flush(struct ly_out *out);
functions.description: Flush any internal output buffers and clean auxiliary data for the given output handler.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.

functions.name: ly_write
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_write(struct ly_out *out, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Write a raw byte buffer into the specified output. After calling, use ly_out_printed() to get the number of bytes written.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.
buf must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
Check the LY_ERR return value; the number of bytes written is available via ly_out_printed(out).

functions.name: ly_out_printed
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL size_t ly_out_printed(const struct ly_out *out);
functions.description: Return the number of bytes printed by the last printing function on this output handler.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.
Must be called after a printing call (ly_print/ly_write or a printer function) to get a meaningful value.

functions.name: ly_out_printed_total
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL size_t ly_out_printed_total(const struct ly_out *out);
functions.description: Return the total number of bytes printed using this output handler since it was created.
requirements: out must be a valid printer handler previously created by one of ly_out_new_*() functions.

functions.name: ly_out_free
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void ly_out_free(struct ly_out *out, void (*clb_arg_destructor)(void *arg), ly_bool destroy);
functions.description: Free a printer handler. Optionally free/close underlying resources depending on the output type and the destroy flag; optionally destroy the callback argument for LY_OUT_CALLBACK using the provided destructor.
requirements: out may be NULL or a valid printer handler to free (behavior for NULL not explicitly documented).
For LY_OUT_MEMORY, if destroy is true, the allocated buffer is freed.
For LY_OUT_FD, LY_OUT_FDSTREAM, and LY_OUT_FILE, if destroy is true, the underlying descriptor/stream is closed.
If the handler is LY_OUT_CALLBACK and clb_arg_destructor is non-NULL, it is used to free the callback argument.

functions.name: lyd_parse_data
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_data(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct lyd_node *parent, struct ly_in *in, LYD_FORMAT format,
        uint32_t parse_options, uint32_t validate_options, struct lyd_node **tree);
functions.description: Parse and optionally validate instance data from an input handler into a libyang data tree. If parent is non-NULL, the input is treated as a subtree and linked under parent. Format may be 0 to auto-detect from the input handler. Validation behavior is controlled by validate_options; parser behavior by parse_options. When parsing subtrees (parent != NULL), only the newly parsed nodes are validated; callers needing full-datastore guarantees should parse all subtrees first and then validate the complete datastore.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid libyang context containing the relevant schemas.
parent is optional; if provided, data are expected to describe a subtree (not necessarily starting at schema root).
in must be a valid ly_in input handle positioned at the start of the data.
format can be 0 to auto-detect; otherwise must be a valid LYD_FORMAT for the input.
parse_options must use only LYD_PARSE_* flags (masked by LYD_PARSE_OPTS_MASK); some flags are mutually exclusive (e.g., LYD_PARSE_STRICT vs LYD_PARSE_OPAQ except LYD_LYB).
validate_options must use only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags (masked by LYD_VALIDATE_OPTS_MASK).
tree must be a valid output pointer; on success it receives the root of the parsed tree (or NULL if the valid result is an empty tree). If parent is set, it receives the first parsed child.
On error, function returns an LY_ERR and additional details can be retrieved via ly_err* APIs from the context.
When parent is non-NULL, only the newly parsed subtree is validated; full cross-tree constraints may not be enforced until a separate full validation is run.

functions.name: lyd_parse_data_mem
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_data_mem(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *data, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t parse_options,
        uint32_t validate_options, struct lyd_node **tree);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around lyd_parse_data() that parses and optionally validates instance data provided in-memory as a null-terminated buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context containing the relevant schemas.
data must point to the input buffer in the specified format; it should be a valid, readable, null-terminated string for text formats.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT (no auto-detect here; unlike lyd_parse_data, 0 is not documented as allowed).
parse_options must use only LYD_PARSE_* flags.
validate_options must use only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
tree must be a valid output pointer; on success it receives the parsed tree root or NULL for an empty but valid result.
On error, returns an LY_ERR; details available via ly_err* APIs.

functions.name: lyd_parse_data_fd
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_data_fd(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, int fd, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t parse_options,
        uint32_t validate_options, struct lyd_node **tree);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around lyd_parse_data() that parses and optionally validates instance data read from a file descriptor referring to a regular file.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context containing the relevant schemas.
fd must be a file descriptor of a regular file; sockets are not supported.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT.
parse_options must use only LYD_PARSE_* flags.
validate_options must use only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
tree must be a valid output pointer; on success it receives the parsed tree root or NULL for an empty but valid result.
On error, returns an LY_ERR; details available via ly_err* APIs.

functions.name: lyd_parse_data_path
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_data_path(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *path, LYD_FORMAT format,
        uint32_t parse_options, uint32_t validate_options, struct lyd_node **tree);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around lyd_parse_data() that parses and optionally validates instance data loaded from a file at the given filesystem path.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context containing the relevant schemas.
path must be a valid path to a readable file containing the input data.
format may be 0 to auto-detect from the file extension, or a specific LYD_FORMAT.
parse_options must use only LYD_PARSE_* flags.
validate_options must use only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
tree must be a valid output pointer; on success it receives the parsed tree root or NULL for an empty but valid result.
On error, returns an LY_ERR; details available via ly_err* APIs.

functions.name: lyd_parse_ext_data
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_ext_data(const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, struct lyd_node *parent, struct ly_in *in,
        LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t parse_options, uint32_t validate_options, struct lyd_node **tree);
functions.description: Parse and optionally validate extension-defined data (e.g., yang-data) limited strictly to the schema tree provided by a specific extension instance. If parent is provided, parsed nodes are attached under it; otherwise a standalone ext-data tree is returned.
requirements: ext must point to a valid extension instance that defines the schema for the data being parsed.
parent is optional; if provided, parsed nodes are connected under parent.
in must be a valid ly_in input handle positioned at the start of the data.
format may be 0 to auto-detect from the input; otherwise must be a valid LYD_FORMAT.
parse_options must use only LYD_PARSE_* flags.
validate_options must use only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
tree must be a valid output pointer; on success it receives the full parsed ext-data tree (may be NULL if empty). If parent is set, tree is set to NULL.
Data must not mix standard module data with extension data; only the extension’s schema tree is allowed.
On error, returns an LY_ERR; details available via context error APIs.

functions.name: lyd_parse_op
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_op(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct lyd_node *parent, struct ly_in *in, LYD_FORMAT format,
        enum lyd_type data_type, uint32_t parse_options, struct lyd_node **tree, struct lyd_node **op);
functions.description: Parse YANG operation-related data (RPC/action requests and replies, notifications, or protocol envelopes) into an operation tree. The function sets specific parsing flags (LYD_PARSE_ONLY, LYD_PARSE_STRICT) and performs no validation; callers may add either of LYD_PARSE_STRICT or LYD_PARSE_OPAQ via parse_options. Behavior and parameter requirements depend on data_type (YANG, NETCONF, RESTCONF variants). For NETCONF/RESTCONF messages, protocol envelopes are returned as an opaque tree via tree while op points to the operation content as applicable.
requirements: At least one of parent, tree, or op must be non-NULL.
ctx must be a valid libyang context.
in must be a valid ly_in positioned at the message start.

format must match the protocol requirements: LYD_XML for NETCONF types; LYD_JSON for RESTCONF notifications; LYD_JSON or LYD_XML for RESTCONF RPC/reply; for pure YANG types, use the expected input format.
data_type must not be LYD_TYPE_DATA_YANG (not accepted).

For LYD_TYPE_RPC_NETCONF: parent must be NULL; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (receives NETCONF envelopes as opaque data, possibly even on failure); op must be provided (operation subtree).
For LYD_TYPE_NOTIF_NETCONF: parent must be NULL; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (envelopes); op must be provided (notification subtree).

For LYD_TYPE_REPLY_NETCONF: parent must be set to the invoked RPC/action node; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (envelopes); op must be NULL; only a data reply appends nodes under the RPC; ok/error replies do not append nodes.

For LYD_TYPE_RPC_RESTCONF: parent must be set to the invoked RPC/action node; format may be LYD_JSON or LYD_XML; tree must be provided (RESTCONF-specific JSON objects as opaque data); op must be NULL (parent identifies the operation).
For LYD_TYPE_NOTIF_RESTCONF: parent must be NULL; format must be LYD_JSON; tree must be provided (RESTCONF-specific JSON objects as opaque data); op must be provided (notification subtree).

For LYD_TYPE_REPLY_RESTCONF: parent must be set to the invoked RPC/action node; format may be LYD_JSON or LYD_XML; tree must be provided (RESTCONF-specific JSON objects as opaque data); op must be NULL; RESTCONF error replies should be parsed as yang-data extension data.
parse_options may include only additions among LYD_PARSE_STRICT or LYD_PARSE_OPAQ to the internally set flags.
On success returns LY_SUCCESS; on protocol root mismatch for NETCONF messages returns LY_ENOT; on other errors returns an LY_ERR and details are available via context error APIs.

functions.name: lyd_parse_ext_op
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_parse_ext_op(const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, struct lyd_node *parent, struct ly_in *in,
        LYD_FORMAT format, enum lyd_type data_type, uint32_t parse_options, struct lyd_node **tree, struct lyd_node **op);
functions.description: Parse extension-defined operation data (e.g., yang-data) according to a specific extension instance, analogous to lyd_parse_op but constrained to the extension’s schema. No validation is performed; specific parameter requirements depend on data_type. For NETCONF replies, only ‘data’ replies append nodes.
requirements: At least one of parent, tree, or op must be non-NULL.
ext must point to a valid extension instance defining the operation schema subtree.
in must be a valid ly_in positioned at the start of the data.
format must match the protocol requirements for the chosen data_type (NETCONF requires LYD_XML).
data_type must be one of the accepted operation types for this API; for NETCONF, the same per-type constraints as in lyd_parse_op apply.
For LYD_TYPE_RPC_NETCONF: parent must be NULL; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (NETCONF envelopes as opaque data); op must be provided (operation subtree).
For LYD_TYPE_NOTIF_NETCONF: parent must be NULL; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (envelopes); op must be provided (notification subtree).
For LYD_TYPE_REPLY_NETCONF: parent must be set to the invoked RPC/action node; format must be LYD_XML; tree must be provided (envelopes); op must be NULL; only data reply appends nodes under the RPC.
parse_options may add either of LYD_PARSE_STRICT or LYD_PARSE_OPAQ to the default flags.
On success returns LY_SUCCESS; on protocol root mismatch for NETCONF messages returns LY_ENOT; otherwise returns LY_ERR on error with details via context error APIs.

functions.name: lyd_validate_ext
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_validate_ext(struct lyd_node **ext_tree, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext,
        uint32_t val_opts, const struct lyd_node *dep_tree, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Validate a standalone extension data tree (independent of normal YANG data) against the schema of a given extension instance. The tree may be modified in-place (nodes may be added/removed) and can become NULL. Optionally returns a diff of changes.
requirements: ext_tree must be a valid pointer to the root pointer of the extension data tree; it may be changed by validation and may become NULL.
ext must be a valid extension instance corresponding to the ext_tree’s schema.
val_opts must contain only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
dep_tree is an optional datastore tree used for validating references from the operation subtree; if provided, it must be a valid libyang data tree.
diff is optional; if provided, it receives a diff of changes performed during validation.
On success returns LY_SUCCESS; otherwise returns an LY_ERR.

functions.name: lyd_validate_all
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_validate_all(struct lyd_node **tree, const struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t val_opts,
        struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Fully validate a complete datastore data tree. The tree is modified in-place (implicit nodes may be added, invalid nodes may be removed and freed). Optionally, a diff of changes is returned.
requirements: tree must be a valid pointer to the root pointer of the data tree; it may be modified in place and may become NULL if validation removes all nodes.
ctx can be NULL if tree is set; otherwise, if provided, it must be a valid libyang context consistent with the tree.
val_opts must contain only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags; behavior can be adjusted (e.g., NO_STATE, PRESENT, MULTI_ERROR, OPERATIONAL, NO_DEFAULTS, NOT_FINAL).
diff is optional; if provided, it receives a diff of validation changes.
On success returns LY_SUCCESS; otherwise returns an LY_ERR.

functions.name: lyd_validate_module
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_validate_module(struct lyd_node **tree, const struct lys_module *module, uint32_t val_opts,
        struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Validate the portion of a data tree belonging to a specific YANG module. The tree is modified in-place and nodes may be added/removed and freed. For validating multiple modules, it is recommended to first validate each with LYD_VALIDATE_NOT_FINAL and then finish with lyd_validate_module_final() per module to avoid false positives due to inter-module dependencies.
requirements: tree must be a valid pointer to the root pointer of the data tree; it may be modified and may become NULL.
module must be a valid pointer to the target YANG module whose data and schema restrictions are to be validated.
val_opts must contain only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags; LYD_VALIDATE_NOT_FINAL is specifically intended for multi-module staged validation.
diff is optional; if provided, it receives a diff of changes made by validation.
On success returns LY_SUCCESS; otherwise returns an LY_ERR.

functions.name: lyd_validate_module_final
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_validate_module_final(struct lyd_node *tree, const struct lys_module *module,
        uint32_t val_opts);
functions.description: Finish validation of a module’s data that were previously validated using LYD_VALIDATE_NOT_FINAL. This finalization does not add or remove any nodes.
requirements: tree must point to the data tree to finalize.
module must be a valid pointer to the YANG module whose data are being finalized.
val_opts must contain only LYD_VALIDATE_* flags.
Caller should have previously validated the module’s data with LYD_VALIDATE_NOT_FINAL before calling this function to avoid incomplete validation states.
Returns LY_SUCCESS on success; otherwise returns an LY_ERR.

functions.name: lyd_validate_op
functions.signature:
LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_validate_op(struct lyd_node *op_tree, const struct lyd_node *dep_tree, enum lyd_type data_type,
        struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Validate an operation subtree (RPC/action input, output, or notification). Only the operation subtree is validated; any parents are ignored. Optional dep_tree may be supplied to resolve references from the operation to datastore content. Optionally returns a diff of changes.
requirements: op_tree must point to the operation tree (or any of its parents); only the operation subtree is validated.
dep_tree is optional; if provided, it must be a valid data tree used to validate references from the operation subtree.
data_type must be one of the YANG operation types (YANG variants only; NETCONF/RESTCONF message types are not accepted for this validation).
diff is optional; if provided, it receives a diff of changes during validation.
Returns LY_SUCCESS on success; otherwise returns an LY_ERR.

functions.name: lys_parse
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lys_parse(struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct ly_in *in, LYS_INFORMAT format, const char **features, struct lys_module **module)
functions.description: Parse a YANG/YIN schema from a libyang input handler and load it into the given context. Use this as the primary parsing API; it performs syntax parsing into internal structures and, if the module is to be implemented, compiles it. The format may be explicitly provided or auto-detected when 0 (LYS_IN_UNKNOWN). Optionally enable features and obtain the resulting module pointer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context instance.
in must be a valid, initialized libyang input handler (struct ly_in) positioned at the schema to parse.
format can be 0 to request auto-detection; otherwise it must be a valid LYS_INFORMAT value (LYS_IN_YANG or LYS_IN_YIN).
features may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must be a NULL-terminated array of feature name strings.
module may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is an output parameter that on success receives the parsed module pointer.
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value to determine success or failure.
On error, output parameters may be left unmodified or set to NULL (unspecified beyond documentation).

functions.name: lys_parse_mem
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lys_parse_mem(struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *data, LYS_INFORMAT format, struct lys_module **module)
functions.description: Convenience helper to parse a schema provided as an in-memory string in the specified format and load it into the context. Prefer lys_parse() for complex scenarios.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context instance.
data must point to a NUL-terminated string containing the entire schema in the specified format.
format must be a valid LYS_INFORMAT value (no auto-detect via 0 is stated here).
module may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is an output parameter that on success receives the parsed module pointer.
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: lys_parse_fd
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lys_parse_fd(struct ly_ctx *ctx, int fd, LYS_INFORMAT format, struct lys_module **module)
functions.description: Convenience helper to read and parse a schema from a file descriptor and load it into the context. Only regular files are supported (not sockets, pipes, etc.). Prefer lys_parse() with a custom input handler for complex use cases.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context instance.
fd must refer to a regular file; sockets, pipes, and non-regular descriptors are not supported.
format must be a valid LYS_INFORMAT value.
module may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is an output parameter that on success receives the parsed module pointer.
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: lys_parse_path
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lys_parse_path(struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *path, LYS_INFORMAT format, struct lys_module **module)
functions.description: Convenience helper to load and parse a schema from a file path in the given format into the context. Prefer lys_parse() with an input handler for complex needs.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libyang context instance.
path must be a valid path to a file containing the schema in the specified format.
format must be a valid LYS_INFORMAT value.
module may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is an output parameter that on success receives the parsed module pointer.
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value.

functions.name: lys_search_localfile
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lys_search_localfile(const char * const *searchpaths, ly_bool cwd, const char *name, const char *revision, char **localfile, LYS_INFORMAT *format)
functions.description: Search recursively for a schema file by name (and optional revision) within provided search paths and optionally in the current working directory. Returns the absolute path to the best match and optionally the expected document format based on file suffix. Returns LY_SUCCESS even if no file is found (then *localfile is set to NULL).
requirements: searchpaths must be a NULL-terminated array of directory paths to search (recursively). It may be NULL to rely solely on cwd searching behavior.
cwd controls whether the current working directory is also searched non-recursively (true to include it).
name must be the schema name to find (non-NULL).
revision may be NULL to request the newest found schema; if non-NULL, only a matching revision is accepted.
localfile is mandatory and must be a valid pointer to a char*; on return, it receives an absolute path to the found schema, or is set to NULL if not found.
format may be NULL; if non-NULL, on success it is set to the expected format (derived from file suffix).
Callers must handle that the function can return LY_SUCCESS with no result; they must check whether *localfile is NULL to distinguish not-found.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned *localfile if the library allocates it (allocation semantics follow libyang conventions; not specified further here).

functions.name: lyd_print_all
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_all(struct ly_out *out, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints the entire data tree starting at root, including all its siblings, to the given output handler in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB). Intended for serializing a complete top-level dataset using a libyang ly_out* output handler.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized libyang output handler created with ly_out_*() and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
root may be any sibling in a top-level set; the function prints the whole sibling set.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options must not include LYD_PRINT_SIBLINGS (this function already prints siblings).
For LYB format, most flags are ignored except LYD_PRINT_SIBLINGS (not applicable here) and LYD_PRINT_SHRINK; LYB printing may require validation when LYD_PRINT_SHRINK is used.
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_tree
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_tree(struct ly_out *out, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints only the subtree rooted at root to the given output handler in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB). Use when you need to serialize a specific subtree without its siblings.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized libyang output handler created with ly_out_*() and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
root must point to the subtree root to print; only that subtree is printed.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options must not include LYD_PRINT_SIBLINGS (this function prints only the subtree).
For LYB format, most flags are ignored except LYD_PRINT_SIBLINGS (not applicable here) and LYD_PRINT_SHRINK; LYB printing may require validation when LYD_PRINT_SHRINK is used.
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_mem
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_mem(char **strp, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Serializes the (sub)tree rooted at root into a newly produced memory buffer in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB) and stores the pointer in strp.
requirements: strp must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* location where the resulting buffer pointer will be stored.
root must point to the (sub)tree root to print.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options may include any defined data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).
Ownership/lifetime and deallocation function for the returned buffer are not specified in this header; consult the library documentation (unknown).
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_fd
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_fd(int fd, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints the (sub)tree rooted at root to the given file descriptor in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB).
requirements: fd must reference a valid, open file descriptor suitable for writing.
root must point to the (sub)tree root to print.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options may include any defined data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_file
