functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_file(FILE *f, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints the (sub)tree rooted at root to the given stdio FILE* in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB).
requirements: f must be a valid FILE* stream opened for writing.
root must point to the (sub)tree root to print.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options may include any defined data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_path
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_path(const char *path, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints the (sub)tree rooted at root to a file at the given filesystem path in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB).
requirements: path must be a non-NULL, valid filesystem path string. The exact file creation/overwrite behavior is not specified here (unknown).
root must point to the (sub)tree root to print.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options may include any defined data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_print_clb
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyd_print_clb(ly_write_clb writeclb, void *user_data, const struct lyd_node *root, LYD_FORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints the (sub)tree rooted at root using a user-provided write callback (semantics akin to write(1)), passing user_data to that callback, in the specified format (XML, JSON, or LYB).
requirements: writeclb must be a valid function conforming to ly_write_clb; it will be called to write out produced bytes.
user_data is optional and may be NULL; it is forwarded to writeclb on each invocation.
root must point to the (sub)tree root to print.
format must be a valid LYD_FORMAT value supported by libyang.
options may include any defined data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).
Callback must correctly handle the provided buffers and return values per ly_write_clb contract (details not specified here; unknown).
Caller must handle the returned LY_ERR and treat non-zero values as errors.

functions.name: lyd_node_should_print
functions.signature: ly_bool lyd_node_should_print(const struct lyd_node *node, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Determines whether a given data node should be printed under the supplied printer options. Returns non-zero if it should be printed, 0 otherwise. Useful for filtering during custom printing or traversal.
requirements: node must be a valid pointer to a libyang lyd_node.
options must be a combination of valid data printer flags (LYD_PRINT_*).

functions.name: lyd_metadata_should_print
functions.signature: ly_bool lyd_metadata_should_print(const struct lyd_meta *meta);
functions.description: Determines whether a given metadata entry should be printed. Returns non-zero if it should be printed, 0 otherwise.
requirements: meta must be a valid pointer to a libyang lyd_meta.

functions.name: lys_print_module
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_print_module(struct ly_out *out, const struct lys_module *module, LYS_OUTFORMAT format, size_t line_length, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints a schema module in the specified format to the provided ly_out output handler. Supports YANG, YANG compiled, YIN, and tree diagram formats. Use ly_out_*() helpers to create/destroy the output handler. line_length applies only to the tree format (0 means unlimited). Returns an LY_ERR status code.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized struct ly_out created via ly_out_*() functions.
module must point to a valid parsed schema module.
format must be a valid LYS_OUTFORMAT value; all listed formats are supported.
line_length is used only with LYS_OUT_TREE; set 0 for unlimited line length.
options must be a combination of schema printer flags (e.g., LYS_PRINT_SHRINK, LYS_PRINT_NO_SUBSTMT) or 0.
Caller must handle the LY_ERR return value (non-zero indicates an error).

functions.name: lys_print_submodule
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_print_submodule(struct ly_out *out, const struct lysp_submodule *submodule, LYS_OUTFORMAT format, size_t line_length, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Prints a schema submodule in the specified format to the provided ly_out handler. Wrapper for printing only a parsed submodule. YANG compiled output is explicitly not supported. line_length applies only to the tree format (0 means unlimited). Returns an LY_ERR status code.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized struct ly_out created via ly_out_*() functions.
submodule must point to a valid parsed submodule.
format must be a valid LYS_OUTFORMAT value and must not be LYS_OUT_YANG_COMPILED (unsupported for submodules).
line_length is used only with LYS_OUT_TREE; set 0 for unlimited line length.
options must be a combination of schema printer flags (e.g., LYS_PRINT_SHRINK, LYS_PRINT_NO_SUBSTMT) or 0.
Caller must handle the LY_ERR return value (non-zero indicates an error).

functions.name: lys_print_mem
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_print_mem(char **strp, const struct lys_module *module, LYS_OUTFORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that prints a schema module to a newly allocated memory buffer in the given format. On success, stores a NUL-terminated string in *strp, which the caller must free() when done. Returns an LY_ERR status code.
requirements: strp must be non-NULL; on success *strp is set to an allocated buffer that must be freed by the caller using free().
module must point to a valid parsed schema module.
format must be a valid LYS_OUTFORMAT value.
options must be a combination of schema printer flags (e.g., LYS_PRINT_SHRINK, LYS_PRINT_NO_SUBSTMT) or 0.
Caller must handle the LY_ERR return value (non-zero indicates an error).

functions.name: lys_print_fd
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_print_fd(int fd, const struct lys_module *module, LYS_OUTFORMAT format, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that prints a schema module to the specified file descriptor in the given format. Returns an LY_ERR status code.

functions.name: ly_set_new
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_new(struct ly_set **set_p);
functions.description: Create and initialize a new ly_set structure and return it via set_p. Use to obtain an empty, reusable set container for storing object pointers. Caller frees it with ly_set_free() (or ly_set_erase() for static instances).
requirements: set_p must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated set.
On success, *set_p points to a valid, empty ly_set instance; caller is responsible for eventually freeing it with ly_set_free().
Caller must check the return value: LY_SUCCESS on success; LY_EINVAL if set_p is NULL; LY_EMEM on allocation failure.

functions.name: ly_set_dup
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_dup(const struct ly_set *set, void *(*duplicator)(const void *obj), struct ly_set **newset_p);
functions.description: Duplicate an existing set. If duplicator is provided, it is called for each object to produce a copy; otherwise, the new set references the same object pointers as the original. Useful for snapshotting or creating an independently managed set.
requirements: set must be a valid pointer to an initialized ly_set (may be empty).
newset_p must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicated set.

If duplicator is provided, it must match signature void *(*)(const void *), accept each object pointer stored in set, and return a pointer to the duplicated object; it must be safe to call once per element.
Caller must check the return value: LY_SUCCESS on success; LY_EINVAL for invalid parameters; LY_EMEM on allocation failure.
If duplicator is NULL, both sets will reference the same object pointers; the caller must avoid double-free by coordinating destructor usage when freeing/erasing either set.

functions.name: ly_set_add
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_add(struct ly_set *set, const void *object, ly_bool list, uint32_t *index_p);
functions.description: Add an object pointer to the set. When list is false, the set behaves as a set and avoids duplicates; if the object already exists, it is not added and index_p (if provided) returns its index. When list is true, duplicates are allowed and treated as a simple list append. Preserves insertion order until removals that relocate the last item.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
object is a pointer value to store; caller controls the concrete type and must keep type consistency within the set.
list controls duplicate handling: set semantics (list==0) avoid duplicates; list semantics (list!=0) allow duplicates.
If index_p is non-NULL, on success it receives the index of the inserted object or the existing object's index if a duplicate was detected (when list==0).
Caller must check the return value: LY_SUCCESS on success; LY_EINVAL on invalid input; LY_EMEM on allocation failure.

functions.name: ly_set_merge
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_merge(struct ly_set *trg, const struct ly_set *src, ly_bool list, void *(*duplicator)(const void *obj));
functions.description: Add all objects from src into trg. When list is false, duplicate elements are ignored to maintain set semantics; when true, all elements are appended allowing duplicates. If duplicator is provided, each object from src is duplicated before adding; otherwise trg will reference the same pointers as src.
requirements: trg must be a valid, initialized target ly_set.
src must be a valid ly_set (may be empty).
list controls duplicate handling: set semantics (list==0) check for and ignore duplicates; list semantics (list!=0) allow duplicates.
If duplicator is provided, it must match void *(*)(const void *), accept each src object pointer, and return a pointer to a duplicate suitable for insertion into trg.
Caller must check the return value: LY_SUCCESS on success; LY_EINVAL for invalid parameters; LY_EMEM on allocation failure.
If duplicator is NULL, resulting sets may share object pointers; the caller must avoid double-free when later destroying sets.

functions.name: ly_set_contains
functions.signature: ly_bool ly_set_contains(const struct ly_set *set, const void *object, uint32_t *index_p);
functions.description: Check whether the set contains the specified object pointer. Optionally returns the index of the found object. Useful to test membership and obtain its current position.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
object is the pointer value to search for (exact pointer equality is used).
If index_p is non-NULL and the object is found, *index_p receives its index.
Return value is a boolean indicating presence; caller should not assume any modification of the set.

functions.name: ly_set_clean
functions.signature: void ly_set_clean(struct ly_set *set, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Remove all objects from the set but keep the set container allocated for further use. If destructor is provided, it is called for each object before it is removed.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept each stored object pointer, and be safe to call once per element.
After the call, set remains valid and empty; caller may continue using it.

functions.name: ly_set_rm
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_rm(struct ly_set *set, void *object, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Remove a specific object pointer from the set (if present). The last element is moved into the removed slot, so remaining element indices may change. If destructor is provided, it is called for the removed object.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
object should be a pointer equal to one stored in the set; removal is based on pointer equality.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept the removed object pointer, and be safe to call once.
Caller must handle potential index changes of other elements after removal.
Caller must check the return value (LY_ERR). Specific codes are not detailed in this header; treat non-zero as failure.

functions.name: ly_set_rm_index
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_rm_index(struct ly_set *set, uint32_t index, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Remove the object at the specified index. The last element is moved to fill the gap, so element order is not preserved and indices of subsequent elements may change. If destructor is provided, it is called for the removed object.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
index must be less than set->count at the time of the call.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept the removed object pointer, and be safe to call once.
Caller must handle potential index changes of other elements after removal due to swap-with-last semantics.
Caller must check the return value (LY_ERR). Specific codes are not detailed in this header; treat non-zero as failure.

functions.name: ly_set_rm_index_ordered
functions.signature: LY_ERR ly_set_rm_index_ordered(struct ly_set *set, uint32_t index, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Remove the object at the specified index while preserving the order of the remaining elements. Items after the removed index are shifted down by one. If destructor is provided, it is called for the removed object.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized ly_set.
index must be less than set->count at the time of the call.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept the removed object pointer, and be safe to call once.
Caller must check the return value (LY_ERR). Specific codes are not detailed in this header; treat non-zero as failure.

functions.name: ly_set_free
functions.signature: void ly_set_free(struct ly_set *set, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Free the ly_set structure and its contents. If destructor is provided, it is called for each stored object; otherwise, only the container and its internal array are freed and the pointed-to objects are left intact.
requirements: set may be NULL (common C convention), but if non-NULL it must be a valid ly_set previously created/initialized.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept each stored object pointer, and be safe to call once per element.
After this call, the set pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: ly_set_erase
functions.signature: void ly_set_erase(struct ly_set *set, void (*destructor)(void *obj));
functions.description: Erase the contents of a statically allocated or stack-embedded ly_set without freeing the ly_set object itself. If destructor is provided, it is called for each stored object. Use for static ly_set instances instead of ly_set_free().
requirements: set must be a valid ly_set object whose storage is managed by the caller (e.g., static or stack); this function does not free the struct itself.
If destructor is provided, it must match void (*)(void *), accept each stored object pointer, and be safe to call once per element.
After the call, the set remains valid and empty for reuse.

functions.name: lyd_new_implicit_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_new_implicit_tree(struct lyd_node *tree, uint32_t implicit_options, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Adds missing implicit nodes into a subtree (non-presence containers and default leaves/leaf-lists as allowed by options). Default-with-false-when are not added. Optionally returns diff of created nodes.
requirements: tree must be a valid subtree root
implicit_options control inclusion of config/state/output/defaults

functions.name: lyd_new_implicit_all
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_new_implicit_all(struct lyd_node **tree, const struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t implicit_options, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Adds missing implicit nodes into a (possibly empty) top-level data set; may change the first-sibling; optionally returns diff.
requirements: If *tree is an empty tree (NULL), ctx must be provided
Caller should re-evaluate first sibling via lyd_first_sibling() if needed

functions.name: lyd_new_implicit_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_new_implicit_module(struct lyd_node **tree, const struct lys_module *module, uint32_t implicit_options, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Adds missing implicit nodes of a specific module into the tree; optionally returns diff.
requirements: module must identify the module whose implicit nodes to create
Caller should re-evaluate first sibling if top-level changed

functions.name: lyd_change_term
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_change_term(struct lyd_node *term, const char *val_str);
functions.description: Changes the value of a leaf/leaf-list to a string value (JSON prefixes) and clears default flag. Returns LY_EEXIST if only default flag cleared, LY_ENOT if equal and no change.
requirements: term must be a leaf or leaf-list node
val_str must be in JSON format for values with prefixes

functions.name: lyd_change_term_bin
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_change_term_bin(struct lyd_node *term, const void *value, uint32_t value_size_bits);
functions.description: Changes the value of a leaf/leaf-list to a binary LYB value and clears default flag.
requirements: term must be a leaf or leaf-list
value must point to binary representation; value_size_bits gives its size

functions.name: lyd_change_term_canon
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_change_term_canon(struct lyd_node *term, const char *val_str);
functions.description: Changes value of a leaf/leaf-list to a canonical-form string (or JSON if none defined) and clears default flag. Non-canonical input may lead to unexpected behavior.
requirements: term must be a leaf or leaf-list
val_str should be canonical (or JSON if canonical not defined)

functions.name: lyd_change_meta
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_change_meta(struct lyd_meta *meta, const char *val_str);
functions.description: Changes the value of a metadata instance using JSON-formatted prefixes where applicable.
requirements: meta must be a valid metadata instance
val_str must be provided in JSON format for prefixed values

functions.name: lyd_insert_child
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_insert_child(struct lyd_node *parent, struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Inserts a node (and any following siblings if it is first in a list) as a child of parent, unlinking from any previous tree and placing per schema order.
requirements: parent must be an inner node that can accept children
node may belong to another tree; it will be unlinked automatically

functions.name: lyd_insert_sibling
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_insert_sibling(struct lyd_node *sibling, struct lyd_node *node, struct lyd_node **first);
functions.description: Inserts node into a siblings list (possibly empty), unlinking from prior location. Returns the first sibling if requested.
requirements: sibling may be NULL to start a new sibling set
node may be first of a sequence; all subsequent will be inserted

functions.name: lyd_insert_before
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_insert_before(struct lyd_node *sibling, struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Inserts node before sibling; only valid for user-ordered nodes. Automatically unlinks node from prior location.
requirements: sibling must be a user-ordered list/leaf-list instance
node must be compatible with sibling's schema

functions.name: lyd_insert_after
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_insert_after(struct lyd_node *sibling, struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Inserts node after sibling; only valid for user-ordered nodes. Automatically unlinks node from prior location.
requirements: sibling must be a user-ordered list/leaf-list instance
node must be compatible with sibling's schema

functions.name: lyd_unlink_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_unlink_siblings(struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Unlinks the specified node and all its following siblings (including their subtrees) from current tree.
requirements: node must be a valid sibling node pointer

functions.name: lyd_unlink_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_unlink_tree(struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Unlinks a data subtree rooted at node from the tree.
requirements: node must be a valid subtree root

functions.name: lyd_free_all
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_all(struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Frees all nodes in a tree (even parents of the provided node).
requirements: node must be any node inside the tree to free

functions.name: lyd_free_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_siblings(struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Frees all sibling nodes (both preceding and succeeding) of the given node.
requirements: node must be any sibling from the set to free

functions.name: lyd_free_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_tree(struct lyd_node *node);
functions.description: Unlinks and frees a data subtree rooted at node.
requirements: node must be the root of the (sub)tree to free

functions.name: lyd_free_meta_single
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_meta_single(struct lyd_meta *meta);
functions.description: Frees a single metadata instance.
requirements: meta must be a valid metadata pointer

functions.name: lyd_free_meta_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_meta_siblings(struct lyd_meta *meta);
functions.description: Frees a metadata instance and all following metadata instances.
requirements: meta must be the first (or any) metadata in a linked sequence

functions.name: lyd_free_attr_single
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_attr_single(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct lyd_attr *attr);
functions.description: Frees a single opaque-node attribute using the context it was created in.
requirements: ctx must be the context where attributes were created
attr must be a valid attribute pointer

functions.name: lyd_free_attr_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyd_free_attr_siblings(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, struct lyd_attr *attr);
functions.description: Frees an attribute and all following attributes using the provided context.
requirements: ctx must be the creation context
attr must be a valid first attribute pointer

functions.name: lyd_value_validate
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_value_validate(const struct lysc_node *schema, const char *value, uint32_t value_len, const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const struct lysc_type **realtype, const char **canonical);
functions.description: Validates whether the given string value conforms to the type restrictions of the given leaf/leaf-list schema. Optionally returns the real type and canonical value.
requirements: value must be provided with explicit length value_len
value is expected in JSON format
ctx_node may be required for types like leafref/instance-identifier; if missing when required, LY_EINCOMPLETE is returned
Caller must free returned canonical (dictionary) using lydict_remove()

functions.name: lyd_value_validate_dflt
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_value_validate_dflt(const struct lysc_node *schema, const char *value, struct lysc_prefix *prefixes, const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const struct lysc_type **realtype, const char **canonical);
functions.description: Validates a default value (lysc_value with stored prefixes) for a leaf/leaf-list schema; similar to lyd_value_validate but accepts stored prefixes.
requirements: value and prefixes come from a lysc_value
ctx_node may be required for leafref/instance-identifier; if missing when required, LY_EINCOMPLETE is returned
Caller must free returned canonical using lydict_remove()

functions.name: lyd_value_compare
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_value_compare(const struct lyd_node_term *node, const char *value, uint32_t value_len);
functions.description: Validates and compares a terminal node's current value against a provided string value (JSON), returning equality or not.
requirements: value must be provided with explicit length
value should be JSON-formatted for prefixed types

functions.name: lyd_compare_single
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_compare_single(const struct lyd_node *node1, const struct lyd_node *node2, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Compares two data nodes for equivalence; options control recursion, default handling, and opaque comparison.
requirements: node1 and node2 may belong to different contexts (supported)
options may include LYD_COMPARE_FULL_RECURSION, LYD_COMPARE_DEFAULTS, LYD_COMPARE_OPAQ

functions.name: lyd_compare_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_compare_siblings(const struct lyd_node *node1, const struct lyd_node *node2, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Compares two sibling lists for equivalence with options similar to lyd_compare_single.
requirements: node1 and node2 may be roots of their sibling sets; contexts may differ

functions.name: lyd_compare_meta
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_compare_meta(const struct lyd_meta *meta1, const struct lyd_meta *meta2);
functions.description: Compares two metadata instances for equivalence. If their contexts differ, they are never equivalent.
requirements: meta1 and meta2 must be valid metadata pointers

functions.name: lyd_dup_single
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_dup_single(const struct lyd_node *node, struct lyd_node_inner *parent, uint32_t options, struct lyd_node **dup);
functions.description: Duplicates a node (optionally recursively and/or with parents) keeping schema references in the same context. Can also copy flags/metadata/private pointers per options.
requirements: node must be a valid data node
If LYD_DUP_WITH_PARENTS and parent is provided, missing parents are duplicated and connected under parent
options control recursion/metadata/flags etc.

functions.name: lyd_dup_single_to_ctx
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_dup_single_to_ctx(const struct lyd_node *node, const struct ly_ctx *trg_ctx, struct lyd_node_inner *parent, uint32_t options, struct lyd_node **dup);
functions.description: Duplicates a node but rebinds schema references to a target context (top-level nodes).
requirements: trg_ctx must be the target context for duplicated nodes
Other requirements as in lyd_dup_single

functions.name: lyd_dup_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_dup_siblings(const struct lyd_node *node, struct lyd_node_inner *parent, uint32_t options, struct lyd_node **dup);
functions.description: Duplicates a node and all following siblings (keeping same context).
requirements: node must be a valid starting sibling
options as per dupoptions

functions.name: lyd_dup_siblings_to_ctx
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_dup_siblings_to_ctx(const struct lyd_node *node, const struct ly_ctx *trg_ctx, struct lyd_node_inner *parent, uint32_t options, struct lyd_node **dup);
functions.description: Duplicates a node and following siblings with schema references resolved in a target context.
requirements: trg_ctx must be the target context
Other requirements as in lyd_dup_siblings

functions.name: lyd_dup_meta_single
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_dup_meta_single(const struct lyd_meta *meta, struct lyd_node *parent, struct lyd_meta **dup);
functions.description: Creates a copy of a metadata instance and attaches it to a parent node.
requirements: meta must be a valid metadata pointer
parent is required as destination

functions.name: lyd_merge_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_merge_tree(struct lyd_node **target, const struct lyd_node *source, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges source data subtree into a top-level target tree. Defaults and metadata handling follow mergeoptions; validation may be needed afterwards.
requirements: *target must point to the first sibling of a top-level tree
source must be a top-level tree
If LYD_MERGE_DESTRUCT set, source will be spent and cannot be reused

functions.name: lyd_merge_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_merge_siblings(struct lyd_node **target, const struct lyd_node *source, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges a top-level source tree (and siblings) into target top-level tree.
requirements: *target must be first sibling of top-level
source must be top-level
LYD_MERGE_* options apply

functions.name: lyd_merge_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_merge_module(struct lyd_node **target, const struct lyd_node *source, const struct lys_module *mod, lyd_merge_cb merge_cb, void *cb_data, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges only nodes of a specific module from source into target, optionally calling a callback for each merged node.
requirements: *target must be first sibling of top-level
source must be top-level
mod may be NULL to include all modules
If subtree added, callback called once with subtree root

functions.name: lyd_diff_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_tree(const struct lyd_node *first, const struct lyd_node *second, uint16_t options, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Computes a diff tree describing differences between two trees as annotated nodes. Diff may be invalid by design; do not validate it.
requirements: first and second must be valid data trees
options may include LYD_DIFF_DEFAULTS/LYD_DIFF_META
Returned diff is independent of inputs and may be NULL if no differences

functions.name: lyd_diff_siblings
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_siblings(const struct lyd_node *first, const struct lyd_node *second, uint16_t options, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Computes a diff for two sibling lists; see lyd_diff_tree for details.
requirements: first and second must be valid sibling sets

functions.name: lyd_diff_apply_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_apply_module(struct lyd_node **data, const struct lyd_node *diff, const struct lys_module *mod, lyd_diff_cb diff_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Applies a diff to data but restricted to a single module (or all if mod is NULL); optional callback per changed node. Beware of duplicate values if diff was created without LYD_DIFF_DEFAULTS and data is not validated after.
requirements: *data must be a modifiable data set
diff must be a valid diff tree
Consider validating resulting tree to consolidate defaults

functions.name: lyd_diff_apply_all
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_apply_all(struct lyd_node **data, const struct lyd_node *diff);
functions.description: Applies a diff to data for all modules.
requirements: *data must be modifiable; diff must be a valid diff

functions.name: lyd_diff_merge_module
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_merge_module(struct lyd_node **diff, const struct lyd_node *src_diff, const struct lys_module *mod, lyd_diff_cb diff_cb, void *cb_data, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges one diff into another restricted to a module; diffs must be mergeable (typically when src_diff was computed on data with target diff applied). Optional callback per merged node.
requirements: *diff is the target diff to merge into; src_diff is the source
mod may be NULL for all modules
options may include LYD_DIFF_MERGE_DEFAULTS

functions.name: lyd_diff_merge_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_merge_tree(struct lyd_node **diff_first, struct lyd_node *diff_parent, const struct lyd_node *src_sibling, lyd_diff_cb diff_cb, void *cb_data, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges source diff siblings into a target diff subtree under diff_parent/diff_first. Optional callback per merged node.
requirements: diff_first/diff_parent denote target location
src_sibling is the source to merge
options as per diffmergeoptions

functions.name: lyd_diff_merge_all
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_merge_all(struct lyd_node **diff, const struct lyd_node *src_diff, uint16_t options);
functions.description: Merges two entire diff trees together.
requirements: *diff is target; src_diff is source
options may include LYD_DIFF_MERGE_DEFAULTS

functions.name: lyd_diff_reverse_all
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_diff_reverse_all(const struct lyd_node *src_diff, struct lyd_node **diff);
functions.description: Creates a reversed diff (creates become deletes, moves reversed, etc.).
requirements: src_diff must be a valid diff
Returns reversed diff via diff

functions.name: lyd_path
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL char *lyd_path(const struct lyd_node *node, LYD_PATH_TYPE pathtype, char *buffer, size_t buflen);
functions.description: Generates a path for the given node in the requested format (standard or without last predicate). Can write into provided buffer or allocate a new string.
requirements: If buffer is NULL, caller must free returned string
If node is disconnected from parents, generated path may be unexpected

functions.name: lyd_find_meta
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL struct lyd_meta *lyd_find_meta(const struct lyd_meta *first, const struct lys_module *module, const char *name);
functions.description: Finds a metadata instance by name (and optional module) starting from the first metadata.
requirements: If module is NULL, name may include a prefix; otherwise, name may not include a prefix

functions.name: lyd_find_sibling_first
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_sibling_first(const struct lyd_node *siblings, const struct lyd_node *target, struct lyd_node **match);
functions.description: Finds the first sibling that is the exact same instance as target (same schema/value), using hashes for performance.
requirements: siblings must reference any node in the sibling list (preceding/succeeding included)
target must be the node instance to match
match may be NULL; otherwise set to found node

functions.name: lyd_find_sibling_val
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_sibling_val(const struct lyd_node *siblings, const struct lysc_node *schema, const char *key_or_value, uint32_t val_len, struct lyd_node **match);
functions.description: Finds in siblings the first instance of a schema node, optionally matching leaf-list value or list keys provided in predicate form. Uses hashes; values are canonized first if applicable.
requirements: schema must not be a key-less list (otherwise LY_EINVAL)
If key_or_value is NULL, returns the first instance of schema
For leaf-list: key_or_value is the searched value (JSON format)
For list: key_or_value is keys predicate string; all keys must be set; order not required
val_len is optional if key_or_value is 0-terminated

functions.name: lyd_find_sibling_dup_inst_set
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_sibling_dup_inst_set(const struct lyd_node *siblings, const struct lyd_node *target, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all exact duplicates of a specific node instance among siblings and returns them in a set (first item is the first instance).
requirements: siblings is any node among the siblings
target is the instance to match
set must be a valid output pointer; empty set returned on LY_ENOTFOUND

functions.name: lyd_find_sibling_opaq_next
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_sibling_opaq_next(const struct lyd_node *first, const char *name, struct lyd_node **match);
functions.description: Finds next opaque node sibling with the specified name.
requirements: first is the first sibling to consider
name is the opaque node name to find

functions.name: lyxp_vars_set
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyxp_vars_set(struct lyxp_var **vars, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Adds or updates an XPath variable in a sized-array of variables; creates a new array when *vars is NULL.
requirements: vars must be a pointer to a variable array pointer
name and value define the variable to add/change

functions.name: lyxp_vars_free
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL void lyxp_vars_free(struct lyxp_var *vars);
functions.description: Frees a sized-array of XPath variables created/used with lyxp_vars_set().
requirements: vars may be NULL or a valid array

functions.name: lyd_find_xpath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_xpath(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath in JSON format on data (starting at ctx_node) and returns a set of matching nodes. Optimized O(1) cases for fully-keyed list/leaf-list selections.
requirements: xpath must evaluate to a node set; otherwise an empty set is returned
set must be a valid output pointer

functions.name: lyd_find_xpath2
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_xpath2(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, const struct lyxp_var *vars, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Like lyd_find_xpath(), but with a sized-array of XPath variables.
requirements: vars may be NULL or a valid variables array

functions.name: lyd_find_xpath3
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_xpath3(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const struct lyd_node *tree, const char *xpath, LY_VALUE_FORMAT format, void *prefix_data, const struct lyxp_var *vars, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: XPath evaluation allowing a separate root tree, and prefix formats other than JSON via format/prefix_data.
requirements: ctx_node may be NULL to indicate root
format and prefix_data must match the prefixes used in xpath

functions.name: lyd_eval_xpath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_eval_xpath(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, ly_bool *result);
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath (JSON format) and returns its boolean value.
requirements: result must be a valid output pointer

functions.name: lyd_eval_xpath2
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_eval_xpath2(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, const struct lyxp_var *vars, ly_bool *result);
functions.description: Like lyd_eval_xpath(), but with XPath variables.
requirements: vars may be NULL or a valid variables array
result must be a valid output pointer

functions.name: lyd_eval_xpath3
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_eval_xpath3(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const struct lys_module *cur_mod, const char *xpath, LY_VALUE_FORMAT format, void *prefix_data, const struct lyxp_var *vars, ly_bool *result);
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath with custom prefix format and current module, returning boolean result.
requirements: cur_mod needed for some formats
format/prefix_data must match prefixes used

functions.name: lyd_eval_xpath4
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_eval_xpath4(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const struct lyd_node *tree, const struct lys_module *cur_mod, const char *xpath, LY_VALUE_FORMAT format, void *prefix_data, const struct lyxp_var *vars, LY_XPATH_TYPE *ret_type, struct ly_set **node_set, char **string, long double *number, ly_bool *boolean);
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath and returns either the raw result type or converts it to a requested type. Either provide ret_type and all result pointers, or exactly one result pointer with obvious type.
requirements: If ret_type is provided, also provide all of node_set, string, number, and boolean
Otherwise, provide exactly one of node_set, string, number, boolean and ret_type is optional
format/prefix_data must correspond to prefixes used in xpath

functions.name: lyd_trim_xpath
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DEF LY_ERR lyd_trim_xpath(struct lyd_node **tree, const char *xpath, const struct lyxp_var *vars);
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath and frees all nodes except the subtrees selected by the expression.
requirements: *tree must be a modifiable data tree
xpath must be valid; vars optional

functions.name: lyd_find_path
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_path(const struct lyd_node *ctx_node, const char *path, ly_bool output, struct lyd_node **match);
functions.description: Finds a node uniquely identified by a simple path starting from ctx_node, in O(depth) time. Ignores/traverses only data nodes (opaque are not traversed).
requirements: path must be a valid simple path
output selects input vs output subtrees for RPC/action nodes
On LY_EINCOMPLETE, match is set to the found parent

functions.name: lyd_find_target
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_find_target(const struct ly_path *path, const struct lyd_node *tree, struct lyd_node **match);
functions.description: Finds the target node referenced by a compiled instance-identifier path within a tree.
requirements: path must be a valid compiled ly_path
tree is the data tree to search in
match may be NULL; otherwise set to found node

functions.name: ly_time_tz_offset
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL int ly_time_tz_offset(void);
functions.description: Returns the current local timezone (including DST) offset from UTC in seconds.

functions.name: ly_time_tz_offset_at
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL int ly_time_tz_offset_at(time_t time);
functions.description: Returns the local timezone (including DST) offset from UTC in seconds at a specific timestamp.
requirements: time is a UNIX timestamp

functions.name: ly_time_str2time
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_time_str2time(const char *value, time_t *time, char **fractions_s);
functions.description: Parses an RFC 3339/YANG date-and-time string into a UNIX timestamp and optional fractions of a second.
requirements: value must contain a valid date-and-time string (may continue past the value)
time must be a valid output pointer
fractions_s may be NULL or will be set to allocated fractions (caller must free per library rules)

functions.name: ly_time_time2str
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_time_time2str(time_t time, const char *fractions_s, char **str);
functions.description: Converts a UNIX timestamp and optional fractions into a canonical date-and-time string in the local timezone.
requirements: str must be a valid output pointer; caller frees the allocated string

functions.name: ly_time_str2ts
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_time_str2ts(const char *value, struct timespec *ts);
functions.description: Parses a YANG date-and-time string into a struct timespec.
requirements: value must be a valid date-and-time string (may continue past the value)
ts must be a valid output pointer

functions.name: ly_time_ts2str
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_time_ts2str(const struct timespec *ts, char **str);
functions.description: Converts a struct timespec into a date-and-time string in the local timezone.
requirements: ts must be a valid pointer
str must be a valid output pointer; caller frees the allocated string

functions.name: lyd_leafref_get_links
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_leafref_get_links(const struct lyd_node_term *node, const struct lyd_leafref_links_rec **record);
functions.description: Returns the leafref links record for the given term node, listing leafrefs pointing to it and targets it points to. Requires LY_CTX_LEAFREF_LINKING context flag.
requirements: node must be a terminal node

record must be a valid output pointer

functions.name: lyd_leafref_link_node_tree
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyd_leafref_link_node_tree(const struct lyd_node *tree);
functions.description: Traverses the data tree and adds leafref links records to nodes. Requires LY_CTX_LEAFREF_LINKING context flag.
requirements: tree must be the data tree root
Context must have LY_CTX_LEAFREF_LINKING enabled

functions.name: ly_pattern_match
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_pattern_match(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *pattern, const char *string, uint32_t str_len, pcre2_code **pcode);
functions.description: Checks whether a string matches an XML Schema regex used in YANG. Optionally uses or returns a compiled PCRE2 code for reuse.
requirements: pattern must be a valid XML Schema regex string
string must be provided; str_len may be 0 if string is 0-terminated
If pcode is non-NULL and *pcode is NULL, a compiled pattern is returned and must be freed with pcre2_code_free()
If pcode is non-NULL and *pcode is non-NULL, it is used directly without compiling

functions.name: ly_pattern_compile
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR ly_pattern_compile(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const char *pattern, pcre2_code **pcode);
functions.description: Compiles an XML Schema regex pattern to a PCRE2 code object for later ly_pattern_match() calls.
requirements: pattern must be a valid XML Schema regex string
pcode must be a valid output pointer; returned code must be freed with pcre2_code_free()

functions.name: lysc_get_type_plugin
functions.signature: struct lyplg_type *lysc_get_type_plugin(uintptr_t plugin_ref);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the type plugin identified by plugin_ref. The reference may be an index into the internal plugin table (indexes start at 1) or a user plugin pointer.
requirements: plugin_ref must either be a valid index (1-based) into libyang's type-plugin array or a valid plugin pointer.
Returns NULL if no plugin matches the reference; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_get_ext_plugin
functions.signature: struct lyplg_ext *lysc_get_ext_plugin(uintptr_t plugin_ref);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the extension plugin identified by plugin_ref. The reference may be an index into the internal plugin table (indexes start at 1) or a user plugin pointer.
requirements: plugin_ref must either be a valid index (1-based) into libyang's extension-plugin array or a valid plugin pointer.
Returns NULL if no plugin matches the reference; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_data_node
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lysc_data_node(const struct lysc_node *schema);
functions.description: Finds the nearest schema ancestor (including the node itself) that has a data-instance (a data node). Returns NULL if the result would be the root (top-level in data).
requirements: schema must point to a valid compiled schema node.
If the returned pointer is NULL, the caller must treat it as top-level.

functions.name: lysc_has_when
functions.signature: const struct lysc_when *lysc_has_when(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Checks whether a compiled schema node’s data instance existence depends on a when condition directly applicable to this node (including direct parent choice/case conditions). Not recursive beyond directly-applicable conditions.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Returns NULL if there is no directly-applicable when condition; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_owner_module
functions.signature: const struct lys_module *lysc_owner_module(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Returns the owner module of a compiled schema node. For augmented nodes, returns the target module (recursively). Otherwise returns the defining module.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return is never NULL for valid schema nodes; if NULL is returned, the input likely was invalid and must be handled.

functions.name: lysp_node_groupings
functions.signature: const struct lysp_node_grp *lysp_node_groupings(const struct lysp_node *node);
functions.description: For a parsed schema node, returns its groupings (linked list) if the node kind supports groupings; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid parsed schema node.
Return may be NULL if the node type has no groupings or none are present; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysp_node_typedefs
functions.signature: const struct lysp_tpdf *lysp_node_typedefs(const struct lysp_node *node);
functions.description: For a parsed schema node, returns its typedefs (sized array) if the node kind supports typedefs; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid parsed schema node.
Return may be NULL if the node type has no typedefs or none are present; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysp_node_actions
functions.signature: const struct lysp_node_action *lysp_node_actions(const struct lysp_node *node);
functions.description: For a parsed schema node, returns its actions/RPCs (linked list) if supported for the node type; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid parsed schema node.
Return may be NULL if not applicable or empty; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysp_node_notifs
functions.signature: const struct lysp_node_notif *lysp_node_notifs(const struct lysp_node *node);
functions.description: For a parsed schema node, returns its notifications (linked list) if supported for the node type; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid parsed schema node.
Return may be NULL if not applicable or empty; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysp_node_child
functions.signature: const struct lysp_node *lysp_node_child(const struct lysp_node *node);
functions.description: For a parsed schema node, returns its first child data node (linked list head) if the node type can have children; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid parsed schema node.
Return may be NULL if the node has no children or does not support children.

functions.name: lysc_node_actions
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node_action *lysc_node_actions(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: For a compiled schema node, returns its actions/RPCs (linked list) if supported for the node type; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return may be NULL if not applicable or empty; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_notifs
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node_notif *lysc_node_notifs(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: For a compiled schema node, returns its notifications (linked list) if supported for the node type; otherwise NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return may be NULL if not applicable or empty; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_child
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lysc_node_child(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: For a compiled schema node, returns its first child schema node (linked list head) if present. Note: choice nodes have only case children; RPC/action nodes have input as first child and output as its sibling.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return may be NULL if there are no children or node does not support children; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_musts
functions.signature: struct lysc_must *lysc_node_musts(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Returns the list (sized array) of must restrictions in a compiled schema node, if present.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return is NULL if there is no must statement in the node; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_when
functions.signature: struct lysc_when **lysc_node_when(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Returns the list (sized array) of pointers to compiled when statements associated with a compiled schema node, if present.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
Return is NULL if there is no when statement in the node; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_lref_target
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lysc_node_lref_target(const struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Returns the single leafref target of a leafref node. For union nodes containing leafrefs, use lysc_node_lref_targets().
requirements: node must refer to a term node of leafref type; otherwise NULL may be returned.
Returns NULL on any error or if no target is found; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_node_lref_targets
functions.signature: LY_ERR lysc_node_lref_targets(const struct lysc_node *node, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Collects the target node(s) of a leafref node or a union node containing leafrefs into a set. The set may be empty if node is of a different type or targets are not found.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled term node.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* variable; on success the set is provided (may be empty).
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value and handle errors.

functions.name: lysc_node_lref_backlinks
functions.signature: LY_ERR lysc_node_lref_backlinks(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_node *node, ly_bool match_ancestors, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all leafref (or union with leafrefs) nodes that target a specific node. If ctx is provided, it is used; otherwise node must be set. If match_ancestors is true, matches also leafrefs targeting ancestors of node.
requirements: Either ctx must be non-NULL or node must be non-NULL.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* variable; on success the set is provided (may be empty).
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value and handle errors.

functions.name: lysc_tree_dfs_full
functions.signature: LY_ERR lysc_tree_dfs_full(const struct lysc_node *root, lysc_dfs_clb dfs_clb, void *data);
functions.description: Performs a DFS traversal of all schema nodes in a (sub)tree including actions and nested notifications, in order: each child subtree, then each action subtree, then each notification subtree. Calls dfs_clb for every visited node.
requirements: root must be a valid schema root/subtree pointer.
dfs_clb must be a valid callback; it may set dfs_continue to skip a subtree.
dfs_clb return value controls traversal termination; caller must handle non-LY_SUCCESS return being propagated.

functions.name: lysc_module_dfs_full
functions.signature: LY_ERR lysc_module_dfs_full(const struct lys_module *mod, lysc_dfs_clb dfs_clb, void *data);
functions.description: Performs a DFS traversal of all schema nodes in a module including RPCs and notifications, calling dfs_clb for each node. Traversal semantics match lysc_tree_dfs_full().
requirements: mod must be a valid module pointer.
dfs_clb must be a valid callback; caller must handle its LY_ERR return value being propagated.

functions.name: lysc_iffeature_value
functions.signature: LY_ERR lysc_iffeature_value(const struct lysc_iffeature *iff);
functions.description: Evaluates a compiled if-feature expression and reports whether it evaluates to true (LY_SUCCESS) or false (LY_ENOT). Returns LY_ERR on error.
requirements: iff must be a valid compiled if-feature pointer.
Caller must handle LY_ENOT for false and other LY_ERR codes for errors.

functions.name: lys_identity_iffeature_value
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_identity_iffeature_value(const struct lysc_ident *ident);
functions.description: Evaluates if-features for a compiled identity. May be called even if the identity has no if-features (returns LY_SUCCESS). Returns LY_ENOT if evaluation is false, LY_ERR on error.
requirements: ident must be a valid compiled identity pointer.
Caller must handle LY_ENOT and other LY_ERR codes.

functions.name: lysp_feature_next
functions.signature: struct lysp_feature *lysp_feature_next(const struct lysp_feature *last, const struct lysp_module *pmod, uint32_t *idx);
functions.description: Iterates over all parsed features of a module and its submodules. Provide last as NULL for the first call, and keep passing the previously returned pointer along with pmod and a submodule index maintained in idx.
requirements: pmod must be a valid parsed module pointer.
On first call, idx must be set to 0.
Returns NULL when iteration is finished; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lys_find_xpath_atoms
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_find_xpath_atoms(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, uint32_t options, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all compiled schema nodes (atoms) required to evaluate a data XPath expression. XPath is expected in JSON-prefix format. Options control access restrictions (see LYS_FIND_XP_* flags).
requirements: Either ctx must be non-NULL for absolute xpath or ctx_node must be non-NULL for relative xpath.
xpath must be a valid, null-terminated string in JSON prefix format.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* for output; caller must handle non-LY_SUCCESS returns.
If options include LYS_FIND_SCHEMAMOUNT and mounted-module nodes are returned, the caller must free their context (as documented by the option).

functions.name: lys_find_expr_atoms
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_find_expr_atoms(const struct lysc_node *ctx_node, const struct lys_module *cur_mod, const struct lyxp_expr *expr, const struct lysc_prefix *prefixes, uint32_t options, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all compiled schema nodes (atoms) required to evaluate a parsed expression. Context node, current module, and compiled prefixes must be provided as applicable. Options control access restrictions (see LYS_FIND_XP_* flags).
requirements: ctx_node may be NULL to use the root as context; otherwise must be a valid compiled node.
cur_mod must be the module where the expression was instantiated.
expr must be a valid parsed XPath expression.
prefixes must be a sized array when required by the expression; may be NULL if not needed.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* for output; caller must handle non-LY_SUCCESS returns.

functions.name: lys_find_xpath
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_find_xpath(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_node *ctx_node, const char *xpath, uint32_t options, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Evaluates a data XPath expression on the schema and returns matching compiled schema nodes. XPath is expected in JSON-prefix format. Options control access restrictions (see LYS_FIND_XP_* flags).
requirements: For absolute xpath, ctx must be non-NULL; for relative xpath, ctx_node must be non-NULL.
xpath must be a valid, null-terminated string in JSON prefix format.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* for output; caller must handle non-LY_SUCCESS returns.
If options include LYS_FIND_SCHEMAMOUNT and mounted-module nodes are returned, the caller must free their context (as documented by the option).

functions.name: lys_find_lypath_atoms
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_find_lypath_atoms(const struct ly_path *path, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all compiled schema nodes (atoms) required to evaluate a compiled ly_path path.
requirements: path must be a valid compiled ly_path pointer.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* for output; caller must handle non-LY_SUCCESS returns.

functions.name: lys_find_path_atoms
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_find_path_atoms(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_node *ctx_node, const char *path, ly_bool output, struct ly_set **set);
functions.description: Finds all compiled schema nodes (atoms) required to evaluate a JSON data path string. Uses ctx for absolute paths or ctx_node for relative ones. If output is set, searches operation output instead of input.
requirements: For absolute path, ctx must be non-NULL; for relative path, ctx_node must be non-NULL.
path must be a valid, null-terminated JSON path string.
set must be a valid pointer to a ly_set* for output; caller must handle LY_ERR return values.

functions.name: lys_find_path
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lys_find_path(const struct ly_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_node *ctx_node, const char *path, ly_bool output);
functions.description: Resolves a JSON data path to a single compiled schema node. Uses ctx for absolute paths or ctx_node for relative ones. If output is set, searches operation output instead of input.
requirements: For absolute path, ctx must be non-NULL; for relative path, ctx_node must be non-NULL.
path must be a valid, null-terminated JSON path string.
Return may be NULL if not found; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lysc_path
functions.signature: char *lysc_path(const struct lysc_node *node, LYSC_PATH_TYPE pathtype, char *buffer, size_t buflen);
functions.description: Generates a schema path string for the given compiled node in the specified format (log/data/data-pattern). If buffer is NULL, the function allocates memory for the full path and the caller must free it.
requirements: node must be a valid compiled schema node.
If buffer is provided, it must point to a writable buffer of length buflen.
If buffer is NULL, the returned string is heap-allocated and the caller is responsible for freeing it.
Returns NULL on memory allocation error; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lys_feature_value
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_feature_value(const struct lys_module *module, const char *feature);
functions.description: Returns the current real status of a feature defined in a module: LY_SUCCESS if enabled, LY_ENOT if disabled, LY_ENOTFOUND if not found. A feature can be considered disabled if its if-features evaluate to false.
requirements: module must be a valid module pointer.
feature must be a valid, null-terminated feature name string.
Caller must handle LY_ENOT and LY_ENOTFOUND results and other LY_ERR codes.

functions.name: lys_getnext
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lys_getnext(const struct lysc_node *last, const struct lysc_node *parent, const struct lysc_module *module, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Iterates schema nodes in schema order that can be instantiated in data. On first call, pass last=NULL and either a parent (to iterate its children) or a module (to iterate top-level). Subsequent calls pass the previously returned node in last. Behavior can be modified via sgetnextflags (e.g., include choice/case, traverse into NP containers, output subtrees, traverse mounted modules).
requirements: If parent is NULL on the first call, module must be specified.
last must be either NULL (first call) or a node previously returned by this function for the same iteration context.

options is a bitmask of sgetnextflags (LYS_GETNEXT_*); if LYS_GETNEXT_WITHSCHEMAMOUNT is used and nodes from mounted modules are returned, the caller must free their context (as documented by the option).
Returns NULL when no further nodes are available; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lys_getnext_ext
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lys_getnext_ext(const struct lysc_node *last, const struct lysc_node *parent, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Iterates extension-provided schema nodes in schema order that can be instantiated in data. Semantics match lys_getnext() but the source is an extension instance instead of a module.
requirements: If parent is NULL on the first call, ext must be specified.
last must be either NULL (first call) or a node previously returned by this function for the same iteration context.
options is a bitmask of sgetnextflags; LYS_GETNEXT_EXT_XPATH differentiates standard traversal vs XPath-accessible tree.
Returns NULL when no further nodes are available; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lys_find_child
functions.signature: const struct lysc_node *lys_find_child(const struct lysc_node *parent, const struct lys_module *module, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint16_t nodetype, uint32_t options);
functions.description: Finds a direct child node matching the specified criteria. If parent is NULL, searches module top-level nodes. Optionally constrain by nodetype bitmask and traversal options (sgetnextflags).
requirements: If parent is NULL, module must be specified (searches top-level of module).
name must be a valid string; if name_len is non-zero it limits the comparison length.
nodetype is an optional bitmask filter; 0 means no filter.
options is a bitmask of sgetnextflags; if LYS_GETNEXT_WITHSCHEMAMOUNT leads to returned nodes from mounted modules, their context must be freed by the caller (as documented by the option).
Returns NULL if no node matches; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: lys_set_implemented
functions.signature: LY_ERR lys_set_implemented(struct lys_module *mod, const char **features);
functions.description: Marks a module as implemented (compiled). If already implemented with a different feature set, the whole context is recompiled. The features array can enable/disable features: '*' enables all; an array of length 1 with only the terminating NULL disables all; NULL leaves features unchanged.
requirements: mod must be a valid module pointer.
features, if provided, must be a NULL-terminated array of strings. Special cases: "*" enables all features; {NULL} disables all features.
Fails with LY_EDENIED if another revision of the same module is already implemented in the context; callers must handle this and other LY_ERR codes.

functions.name: lys_nodetype2str
functions.signature: const char *lys_nodetype2str(uint16_t nodetype);
functions.description: Returns a constant string naming the schema node type corresponding to the nodetype bit value.
requirements: nodetype must be a valid nodetype value; returns a constant string.
The returned pointer is constant storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: lyxp_get_expr
functions.signature: const char *lyxp_get_expr(const struct lyxp_expr *path);
functions.description: Returns the original string representation of a parsed XPath expression object.
requirements: path must be a valid parsed expression pointer.
The returned pointer refers to internal/original storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ly_realloc
functions.signature: void *ly_realloc(void *ptr, size_t size);
functions.description: Wrapper around realloc() that, on allocation failure, also frees the original memory block. Use it to resize a previously heap-allocated block or to allocate when ptr is NULL. Returns a pointer to the resized block on success, or NULL on error. Note: unlike standard realloc(), the original memory is not preserved on failure; it is freed. Behavior for size == 0 is not documented here.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer to a heap block obtained via a compatible allocator (e.g., malloc/calloc/realloc/ly_realloc) and currently valid to reallocate.
size is the requested size in bytes for the resulting allocation; behavior when size == 0 is unspecified in this header (unknown), avoid passing 0 unless implementation is verified.
On allocation failure, the function returns NULL and frees the original block; the caller must not access or free the original pointer after the call if the return value is NULL.
If the function succeeds, the returned pointer owns the allocated memory and must be released with free() when no longer needed.
Do not use the input pointer after the call unless the return value is non-NULL (the location may change on success and is freed on failure).

functions.name: lyplg_add
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyplg_add(const char *pathname);
functions.description: Manually loads a plugin shared object (file) that may contain type and/or extension plugins. Plugins are only loadable when at least one libyang context exists; loaded plugins are tied to the lifetime of contexts and are unloaded when the last context is destroyed. Manually added plugins are appended with the lowest priority among already loaded plugins. Usage: pass the filesystem path to the plugin file; check the LY_ERR return code for success or the specific failure reason.
requirements: At least one libyang context must exist prior to calling this function (otherwise LY_EDENIED is returned).
pathname must be non-NULL (NULL yields LY_EINVAL).
The referenced file must be loadable by the system dynamic loader (otherwise LY_ESYS is returned).
The plugin content must be valid and compatible with the current libyang version (otherwise LY_EINVAL is returned).
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: lyplg_add_extension_plugin
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyplg_add_extension_plugin(struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t version, const struct lyplg_ext_record *recs);
functions.description: Manually registers extension plugins from memory (plugin records) instead of loading a shared object. If ctx is NULL, the plugin is shared among all existing contexts; otherwise it is associated with the provided context. Plugins are only loadable when at least one context exists; they are unloaded when the last context is destroyed. Manually added plugins are appended with the lowest priority. Usage: provide the expected record version and a NULL-terminated (zeroed record) array of lyplg_ext_record entries; check the LY_ERR return code.
requirements: At least one libyang context must exist prior to calling this function (otherwise LY_EDENIED is returned).
ctx may be NULL to share the plugin among all existing contexts; if non-NULL, it must point to a valid, initialized libyang context.
version must match a plugin record version compatible with the running libyang (success only if the versions are compatible).
recs must be non-NULL (NULL yields LY_EINVAL).
recs must be an array terminated by a zeroed record (termination is required for correct processing).
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: lyplg_add_type_plugin
functions.signature: LIBYANG_API_DECL LY_ERR lyplg_add_type_plugin(struct ly_ctx *ctx, uint32_t version, const struct lyplg_type_record *recs);
functions.description: Manually registers type plugins from memory (plugin records) instead of loading a shared object. If ctx is NULL, the plugin is shared among all existing contexts; otherwise it is associated with the provided context. Plugins are only loadable when at least one context exists; they are unloaded when the last context is destroyed. Manually added plugins are appended with the lowest priority. Usage: provide the expected record version and a NULL-terminated (zeroed record) array of lyplg_type_record entries; check the LY_ERR return code.
requirements: At least one libyang context must exist prior to calling this function (otherwise LY_EDENIED is returned).
ctx may be NULL to share the plugin among all existing contexts; if non-NULL, it must point to a valid, initialized libyang context.
version must match a plugin record version compatible with the running libyang (success only if the versions are compatible).
recs must be non-NULL (NULL yields LY_EINVAL).
recs must be an array terminated by a zeroed record (termination is required for correct processing).
Callers must check the LY_ERR return value and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_parse_log
functions.signature: void lyplg_ext_parse_log(const struct lysp_ctx *pctx, const struct lysp_ext_instance *ext, LY_LOG_LEVEL level, LY_ERR err, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a message from an extension plugin during parsing using the parsed extension instance for context/path generation. Intended for use inside extension-parse callbacks.
requirements: pctx should be a valid libyang parse context associated with the currently parsed module (inferred from purpose).
ext should point to the parsed extension instance being processed (inferred from purpose).
format must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match it (standard varargs requirement, inferred).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_parse_get_cur_pmod
functions.signature: const struct lysp_module *lyplg_ext_parse_get_cur_pmod(const struct lysp_ctx *pctx);
functions.description: Returns the current (local) parsed module from a parse context.
requirements: pctx must be a valid parse context obtained from libyang parsing.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_parse_extension_instance
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyplg_ext_parse_extension_instance(struct lysp_ctx *pctx, struct lysp_ext_instance *ext);
functions.description: Parses known substatements of an extension instance into standard parsed schema structures using libyang’s parser. Plugins call this when the extension’s substatements can be parsed in the standard way.
requirements: pctx must be a valid parse context.
ext must be a valid parsed extension instance with its lysp_ext_instance.substmts array prepared; the function updates it by storing parsed data.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_log
functions.signature: void lyplg_ext_compile_log(const struct lysc_ctx *cctx, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, LY_LOG_LEVEL level, LY_ERR err, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a message from an extension plugin during compilation using the compiled extension instance and optional compile context for path generation.
requirements: cctx may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid compile context (from documentation).
ext must refer to the compiled extension instance used for context in logging.
format must be a valid printf-style format string with matching variadic arguments (standard varargs requirement, inferred).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_log_path
functions.signature: void lyplg_ext_compile_log_path(const char *path, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, LY_LOG_LEVEL level, LY_ERR err, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a message from an extension plugin during compilation using an explicit schema path string instead of deriving it from a context.
requirements: path must point to a valid null-terminated schema path string to be logged.
ext must refer to the compiled extension instance used for context in logging.
format must be a valid printf-style format string with matching variadic arguments (standard varargs requirement, inferred).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_log_err
functions.signature: void lyplg_ext_compile_log_err(const struct ly_err_item *eitem, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext);
functions.description: Logs a message from an extension plugin during compilation using a prepared error item and the compiled extension instance.
requirements: eitem must point to a valid libyang error item to log.
ext should be the relevant compiled extension instance to provide context.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_get_ctx
functions.signature: struct ly_ctx *lyplg_ext_compile_get_ctx(const struct lysc_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the libyang context associated with a schema compilation context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compilation context.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_get_options
functions.signature: uint32_t *lyplg_ext_compile_get_options(const struct lysc_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the compilation options flags so they can be read or modified using scflags.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compilation context.
Only scflags-compatible bits should be modified (from documentation).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_get_cur_mod
functions.signature: const struct lys_module *lyplg_ext_compile_get_cur_mod(const struct lysc_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the current module in a schema compilation context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compilation context.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_get_pmod
functions.signature: struct lysp_module *lyplg_ext_compile_get_pmod(const struct lysc_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the currently processed parsed module (lysp_module) from a compilation context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compilation context.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compile_extension_instance
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyplg_ext_compile_extension_instance(struct lysc_ctx *ctx, const struct lysp_ext_instance *extp, struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, struct lysc_node *parent);
functions.description: Compiles substatements of an extension instance using libyang’s standard schema compiler into compiled schema structures. Used when substatements should be compiled in the standard way (possibly influenced by scflags).
requirements: ctx must be a valid compile context.
extp must be the parsed representation of the extension instance being processed.
ext must be a prepared compiled extension instance with its lysc_ext_instance.substmts array prepared; the function updates it by storing compiled data.
parent is an optional schema parent to use for compiled nodes; may be NULL.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_compiled_node_augments
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyplg_ext_compiled_node_augments(struct lysc_ctx *ctx, struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, struct lysc_node *node);
functions.description: Applies augments, if any, to a specific compiled schema node within an extension instance. Useful when virtual nodes cannot be compiled via the standard compile helper.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compile context.
ext must be the compiled extension instance whose augments apply.
node must be a valid compiled schema node to which augments may apply.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_print_get_out
functions.signature: struct ly_out **lyplg_ext_print_get_out(const struct lyspr_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns the output handler pointer location from a YANG printer context so the handler can be read or replaced.
requirements: ctx must be a valid YANG printer context.
The returned pointer points to the handler pointer stored in the context (from documentation).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_print_get_options
functions.signature: uint32_t *lyplg_ext_print_get_options(const struct lyspr_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the printer options flags so they can be read or modified using schemaprinterflags.
requirements: ctx must be a valid YANG printer context.
Only schemaprinterflags-compatible bits should be modified (from documentation).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_print_get_level
functions.signature: uint16_t *lyplg_ext_print_get_level(const struct lyspr_ctx *ctx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current printer indentation level so it can be read or adjusted.
requirements: ctx must be a valid YANG printer context.

functions.name: lyplg_ext_print_info_extension_instance
functions.signature: void lyplg_ext_print_info_extension_instance(struct lyspr_ctx *ctx, const struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, ly_bool *flag);
functions.description: Prints substatements of an extension instance in the INFO (compiled YANG) format using YANG printer helpers. Helps implement the printer_info callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid YANG printer context.
ext must be a valid compiled extension instance whose substatements and nested extensions may be printed.
flag is an in/out boolean indicating whether an opening '{' has already been printed (0 = not yet, 1 = already).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_add_ext_nodes
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_add_ext_nodes(const struct lyspr_tree_ctx *ctx, struct lysc_ext_instance *ext, lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_override_clb clb);
functions.description: Registers a group of compiled schema nodes that already belong to the extension instance to be printed in a tree diagram. An optional override callback can modify each node’s printed form.
requirements: ctx must be a valid printer_tree context.
ext must be the compiled extension instance whose nodes will be printed.
clb is an override callback applied to each node and may be NULL only if not required by the printer (not explicitly stated).

functions.name: lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_add_nodes
functions.signature: LY_ERR lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_add_nodes(const struct lyspr_tree_ctx *ctx, struct lysc_node *nodes, lyplg_ext_sprinter_ctree_override_clb clb);
